data.title: New adaptive optics shows details of our star's atmosphere
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 科学家开发了一种新的“日冕自适应光学系统”，首次拍摄到太阳日冕层的最清晰图像和视频。该系统安装在美国新泽西理工学院运营的1.6米Goode太阳望远镜上，能够消除地球大气湍流造成的图像模糊。这些高分辨率图像展示了日冕中精细结构的快速变化，包括日珥的重组和等离子体流的形成与崩溃，还首次清晰捕捉到“日冕雨”现象，即冷却的等离子体凝结后落回太阳表面。这些观测为研究日冕加热、太阳爆发和空间天气提供了新的视角，并可能带来更多科学发现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳观测技术及其相关科学现象的讨论

不同观点：
• Adam认为，文章中最有趣的创新并不是可变形镜面，而是聚焦于日冕特征的波前传感器设计，这与之前的系统聚焦于太阳表面的“颗粒”不同。
• Itishappy感叹观测的视野规模之大，表现出对天文尺度的惊叹。
• Krunck被第一视频中的稳定结构所吸引，指出虽然整体结构保持不变，但其内部却充满动态变化。
• So-rose表达了对观测太阳表面现象（如太阳针状体）的兴奋，并提到这些现象的物理机制仍在激烈争论中。
• Srean提到自适应光学技术起源于SDI资助的秘密空间武器研究，并指出这一技术曾在不同领域被独立提出。
• Tomrod简单表达了对视频美丽程度的赞赏。
• Whatshisface呼吁观众通过联系国会议员来支持此类研究。
• Ambicapter提出是否可以通过在人造卫星上设置可重新定位的光源来校准和获取更精确的大气畸变数据。
• Jeremyscanvic对其同事在理论天文成像研究中的工作表示赞赏，并认为这种下游应用非常有趣。
• Kadushka质疑“最清晰的图像”为何不是来自更接近太阳的空间拍摄。
• Casenmgreen的评论与其他讨论无关，提到阻止Tor用户。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及的科学机制包括太阳针状体的物理机制，这一机制仍是科学界争论的焦点。
- 技术的历史背景也被提及，特别是自适应光学技术与秘密武器研究的历史渊源。
- 有对天文观测规模的感叹，以及对未来可能的技术改进（如人造星或卫星光源）的设想。
- 不同观众对同一视频内容的关注点各异，从技术细节到政策呼吁，再到纯粹的美学欣赏。

44147573.article_content:
“Raindrops in the Sun’s Corona”: New Adaptive Optics Shows Stunning Details of our Star’s Atmosphere
Credit: Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
Home
»
“Raindrops in the Sun’s Corona”: New Adaptive Optics Shows Stunning Details of our Star’s Atmosphere
Release Date:
May 27, 2025
Scientists from the U.S. National Science Foundation National Solar Observatory and New Jersey Institute of Technology produced the finest images of the Sun’s corona to date. To make these high-resolution images and movies, the team developed a new ‘coronal adaptive optics’ system that removes blur from images caused by the Earth’s atmosphere. Their ground-breaking results were recently published in Nature Astronomy and pave the way for deeper insight into coronal heating, solar eruptions, and space weather, and open an opportunity for new discoveries in the Sun’s atmosphere.
Scientists develop new optical system that removes blur over fine-structure in the Sun’s corona, revealing clearest images to date
BOULDER, CO, Tuesday, May 27, 2025
–
The Sun’s corona—the outermost layer of its atmosphere, visible only during a total solar eclipse—has long intrigued scientists due to its extreme temperatures, violent eruptions, and large prominences. However, turbulence in the Earth’s atmosphere has caused image blur and hindered observations of the corona. A ground-breaking recent development by scientists from the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) National Solar Observatory (NSO), and New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT), is changing that by using adaptive optics to remove the blur.
As published in
Nature Astronomy
, this pioneering ‘coronal adaptive optics’ technology has produced the most astonishing, clearest images and videos of fine-structure in the corona to date. This development will open the door for deeper insights into the corona’s enigmatic behavior and the processes driving space weather.
Most Detailed Coronal Images to Date Revealed
Funded by the NSF and installed at the 1.6-meter Goode Solar Telescope (GST), operated by NJIT’s Center for Solar-Terrestrial Research (CSTR) at Big Bear Solar Observatory (BBSO) in California, “Cona”—the adaptive optics system responsible for these new images—compensates for the blur caused by air turbulence in the Earth’s atmosphere —similar to the bumpy air passengers feel during a flight.
“The turbulence in the air severely degrades images of objects in space, like our Sun, seen through our telescopes. But we can correct for that,”
says Dirk Schmidt, NSO Adaptive Optics Scientist who led the development.
Among the team’s remarkable observations is a movie of a quickly restructuring solar prominence unveiling fine, turbulent internal flows. Solar prominences are large, bright features, often appearing as arches or loops, extending outward from the Sun’s surface.
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Prominence-1-Video.mp4
This image of a prominence above the solar surface is a snapshot of a 4-minute time-lapse movie that reveals its rapid, fine, and turbulent restructuring with unprecedented detail. The Sun’s fluffy-looking surface is covered by “spicules”, short-lived plasma jets, whose creation is still the subject of scientific debate. The streaks on the right of this image are coronal rain falling down onto the Sun’s surface. This image was taken by the Goode Solar Telescope at Big Bear Solar Observatory using the new coronal adaptive optics system Cona. The image shows the hydrogen-alpha light emitted by the solar plasma. The image is artificially colorized, yet based on the color of hydrogen-alpha light, and darker color is brighter light. Credit: Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
A second movie replays the rapid formation and collapse of a finely structured plasma stream.
“These are by far the most detailed observations of this kind, showing features not previously observed, and it’s not quite clear what they are,”
says Vasyl Yurchyshyn, co-author of the study and NJIT-CSTR research professor. “
It is super exciting to build an instrument that shows us the Sun like never before,
” Schmidt adds.
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Plasmoid-Video.mp4
This image was taken by the Goode Solar Telescope at Big Bear Solar Observatory using the new coronal adaptive optics system Cona. The image shows the hydrogen-alpha light emitted by the solar plasma. The image is artificially colorized, yet based on the color of hydrogen-alpha light, and darker color is brighter light.
Credit:
Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
A third movie shows fine strands of coronal rain—a phenomenon where cooling plasma condenses and falls back toward the Sun’s surface. “
Raindrops in the Sun’s corona can be narrower than 20 kilometers,”
NSO Astronomer Thomas Schad concludes from the most detailed images of coronal rain to date, “
These findings offer new invaluable observational insight that is vital to test computer models of coronal processes.
”
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Coronal-Rain-Vi

data.title: Codex CLI is going native
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: OpenAI宣布将Codex CLI工具重写为Rust版本，以提升跨平台稳定性、安全性、性能和可扩展性。目前Codex CLI基于Node.js，存在一些依赖和性能问题，新版本旨在解决这些问题，包括实现零依赖安装、原生安全绑定和优化性能。开发者可以通过运行指定命令试用新版Codex CLI。团队将继续修复TypeScript版本的问题，并逐步使Rust版本在功能上与其看齐。未来计划整合TypeScript和Python等语言支持，并邀请社区贡献者加入。如有问题或反馈，可联系维护团队。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕不同编程语言、工具和生态系统的选择及其重写的讨论，包括背后的技术与非技术原因。

不同观点：
• [wiseowise, tptacek, pjmlp, ThouYS] 认为从解释型语言（如Python、JavaScript）转向原生编译语言（如Go/Rust）是一种回潮趋势。这种趋势的动机部分是为了提升性能和避免Node.js等工具的安装麻烦。有人认为Node.js从一开始就是奇怪的选择。
• [crop_rotation, adsharma, geertj] 讨论了Codex（由OpenAI开发的代码生成工具）与Claude Code的比较，以及Codex是否能自我重写。有人质疑Codex能否在没有人类干预的情况下完成重写任务。
• [quotemstr] 提出语言选择往往与其他技术选择（如内存管理、编译机制、工具集和类型系统严格性）混为一谈。他指出Go的垃圾回收机制表现不错，因此不能简单地说手动内存管理就一定比垃圾回收快。他还强调，语言选择不仅仅是技术偏好，还代表了开发者文化。
• [vendiddy, jbellis] 提到性能问题，特别是桌面客户端（如ChatGPT）的卡顿问题，认为性能优化是选择不同语言或工具链的一个重要原因。
• [CGamesPlay, light_hue_1] 认为OpenAI可能以Rust重写为借口，实际上是为了转向闭源策略，减少开放性。

补充讨论：
• [phito, npalli] 对JavaScript/TypeScript开发CLI工具表示怀疑，认为未来可能会再次出现大规模重写和改变技术栈的趋势。同时，有人警告说，未来维护大量Rust代码也可能成为新的挑战。

争议焦点：
• 重写是否仅仅出于技术需求（如性能、易于部署）还是为了非技术原因（如闭源策略）。
• 不同开发者社区对语言选择的强烈认同感和文化归属感，导致语言争论往往变得激烈。

总结：讨论反映了技术社区对编程语言和工具链选择的复杂性，不仅涉及技术性能，还涉及开发者文化、历史选择和商业策略等多重因素。

Hello! Thank you all for the excitement, feedback, and contributions over the past month or so since launch. It's been incredible to hear from all of you building with Codex CLI and now Codex in ChatGPT
1
Special thank you to all the contributors who opened PRs to improve the CLI for everyone. From fixing bugs to adding features, it's been a lot of fun co-developing this with all of you. We wanted to share an update on a few recurring themes: cross-platform stability, security, performance, and extensibility.
We're continuing to address feedback and fix issues that we hear from the community, while we've been working on a rewrite of Codex CLI into Rust. You can try it today by running:
npm i -g @openai/codex@native
codex
If you're a TypeScript developer like me, you're probably wondering why would we do this. High-level: we want to use the best tool for the job. While Codex CLI ships with a neat terminal UI, which has been easy to whip up and iterate with React-based
ink
2
- the core of this project is an "agentic" harness, aka calling the model in a loop.
Our goal is to make the software pieces as efficient as possible and there were a few areas we wanted to improve:
Zero-dependency Install
— currently Node v22+ is required, which is frustrating or a blocker for some users
Native Security Bindings
— surprise! we already ship a Rust for linux sandboxing since the bindings were available
Optimized Performance
— no runtime garbage collection, resulting in lower memory consumption
Extensible Protocol
— we've been working on a "wire protocol" for Codex CLI to allow developers to extend the agent in different languages (including Type/JavaScript, Python, etc) and MCPs (
already supported in Rust
)
We're planning to continue merging bugfixes in the TypeScript implementation, while we get the Rust implementation to experience and feature parity in the coming weeks. We'll share more updates soon on how TypeScript and other languages like Python will fit in long-term into this project.
If working in Rust, contributing to codex-cli, and building new modes of agentic coding is exciting to you - we're growing our team! Please reach out to us at:
codex-maintainers@openai.com
We're excited to hear your feedback on the new version of Codex CLI as we work towards making it the default experience in the coming weeks. Happy building!

data.title: A new generation of Tailscale access controls
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: Tailscale推出了新一代访问控制系统——Grants，简化了原有的ACL语法，将网络和应用程序权限整合到一个语法中。Grants不仅更容易编写和阅读，还允许定义应用程序能力，通过tsnet库将身份验证和授权集中管理。应用能力是以JSON对象形式定义的权限，可以指定源字段中实体的权限。以Golink为例，通过Grants可以集中管理网络访问和用户角色，无需在应用内维护额外用户数据库。Tailscale提供了tsnet库，帮助开发者读取用户身份和权限，简化授权决策。Grants使网络和应用权限管理更加统一和简便。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tailscale的功能、安全性、易用性及与替代方案的比较

不同观点：
• [mrbluecoat] 认为Tailscale对原有ACL语法提供永久支持，体现了平台的稳定性，并赞赏Tailscale在与开发者社区互动中的表现，预测其将因此继续增长受欢迎度。
• [codethief] 关注Tailnet Lock功能的扩展，希望能够签署tailnet策略文件，以防止在节点和协调服务器被攻陷时，攻击者修改策略文件访问敏感服务如SSH。
• [tpetry] 支持Tailnet Lock功能，但希望Tailscale能引入“ paranoid mode”，要求所有网络变更必须从受信任节点授权，以确保Tailscale无法擅自更改用户网络。同时承认Tailscale比竞争对手有优势，但仍有改进空间。
• [ttul] 提到Tailscale已成为其公司最大的SaaS支出，暗示Tailscale的商业模式有效。
• [bb88] 批评Tailscale在Linux上的配置复杂，特别是netfilter规则，认为它不适合需要高度控制网络配置的用户。
• [dataangel] 关注用户体验的改进，希望Tailscale支持同时连接多个tailnet，并在从休眠恢复后自动重连。
• [nikisweeting] 询问未来是否会有管理授权（grants）的UI界面，以避免手动编写配置。
• [a_t48] 提到Tailscale SSH功能中缺乏轻松获取用户邮箱或用户名的方法，并将其与teleport的优势对比。
• [aatd86] 关注文档示例中的标点使用问题，特别是JSON格式中逗号的使用一致性。

A new generation of Tailscale access controls
Grants are generally available as an easier option to write and read than ACL syntax. Anything you can write as an ACL can be expressed as a grant, coexisting in perfect harmony.
Today, we’re announcing the general availability of grants, Tailscale’s next generation of access controls that combine network and application capabilities into a single syntax.
Grants are a superset of our original ACLs — anything you can write as an ACL can be expressed as a grant. In most scenarios, grants are easier to write and read than the ACL syntax. Let’s take a look:
// ACL syntax
"acls"
:
[
{
"action"
:
"accept"
,
"src"
:
[
"group:eng"
]
,
"dst"
:
[
"tag:internal-tool:443"
]
,
"proto"
:
[
"tcp"
]
}
]
,
// Grants syntax
"grants"
:
[
{
"src"
:
[
"group:eng"
]
,
"dst"
:
[
"tag:internal-tool"
]
"ip"
:
[
"tcp:443"
]
}
]
Grants are designed to be easy to write and easy to read, for both humans and computers. We combined ports and protocols into a single
ip
field, and removed the redundant
action
field. This simplifies our original ACL syntax, where these fields were needed in every rule.
The new stuff
Grants go beyond simplifying the ACL syntax, they also add new tools that you can use for more powerful access controls.
Application capability extensions
Tailscale’s access controls have always been able to define network-level permissions at
Layer 3
, but this is only half the story — you still need to handle authentication and authorization for users once their packets reach your applications.
For private services inside your tailnet, like internal tools, implementing auth on every app is overkill. That’s why we developed
tsnet
, a Go library that embeds Tailscale directly in your applications. This lets you see and react to the identity of every user who makes a request to your app. So, authentication is handled…what about authorization?
That’s where grants come in. You define application capabilities in a grant, and they’re passed to your application. There, you can read them alongside the identity of the user. Together, grants and
tsnet
let you build private services that rely on Tailscale's
RBAC policy expansion
for authentication and authorization.
Application capabilities are namespaced, freeform JSON objects. You can define permissions that should be granted to the entities in the
src
field of your grant. Tailscale has defined a schema in some of our own apps, but you’re not limited to that. The magic of application capabilities is that you can easily define your own capabilities to use in your apps.
Let’s look at
Golink
, a tiny internal shortlink service we use every day at Tailscale. Users in Golink are authenticated with their Tailscale identity, and there are normal users and admin users. We can use grants to not only determine who is allowed to access the Golink service, but also to assign the admin role to specific groups of users:
{
"grants"
:
[
{
// All users in the tailnet can access Golink
"src"
:
[
"autogroup:member"
]
,
"dst"
:
[
"tag:golink"
]
,
"ip"
:
[
"*"
]
}
,
{
// Only the golink-admins group gets Admin privileges in the app
"src"
:
[
"group:golink-admins"
]
,
"dst"
:
[
"tag:golink"
]
,
"app"
:
{
"tailscale.com/cap/golink"
:
[
{
"admin"
:
true
}
]
}
}
]
}
Instead of managing network access to Golink in Tailscale and implementing user role management inside the Golink app, we can centralize both policies in Tailscale. Every request made to Golink includes the Tailscale identity of the requestor and the permissions to grant to that user. This makes it easy to read those properties in the app, making authentication and authorization decisions without maintaining yet another user database.
Here’s what that looks like on the Golink side, using our
tsnet library
:

`json:"admin"`

bool

(

*

.

[

]
(

,

for
_

:=

{

44128751.article_summary: Tailscale推出了新一代访问控制系统——Grants，简化了原有的ACL语法，将网络和应用程序权限整合到一个语法中。Grants不仅更容易编写和阅读，还允许定义应用程序能力，通过tsnet库将身份验证和授权集中管理。应用能力是以JSON对象形式定义的权限，可以指定源字段中实体的权限。以Golink为例，通过Grants可以集中管理网络访问和用户角色，无需在应用内维护额外用户数据库。Tailscale提供了tsnet库，帮助开发者读取用户身份和权限，简化授权决策。Grants使网络和应用权限管理更加统一和简便。

data.title: Learning from the Amiga API/ABI
data.author: danny00
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了从Amiga操作系统API/ABI中可以学到的设计理念，特别是其直接调用共享库的方式，无需运行时链接。Amiga ABI通过一个已知位置的分支指令表实现函数调用，核心库`Exec.library`提供获取其他库函数地址的接口。该ABI不依赖特定CPU，兼容现代内存保护机制，适用于多种编程语言。文章还介绍了Amiga OS的其他优点，如内核的列表管理、消息传递和多任务处理，以及`Intuition`窗口系统的异步事件处理能力。相比现代操作系统，Amiga OS的设计更加简洁和易用。此外，文章提到AmigaDOS及其替代库ARP的演变，展示了Amiga OS库系统的灵活性。总体而言，Amiga OS的ABI设计在今天仍然具有借鉴意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AmigaOS的设计优雅性、技术特点及其对后续系统的影响

不同观点：
• flohofwoe认为AmigaOS是他见过的最优雅的软件设计之一，尤其是其通过从固定地址（ExecBase）引导整个系统的设计。他还指出，由于工期压力加入的DOS部分比较丑陋。整体系统数据结构通过链表连接，虽然安全性差，但非常适合学习和扩展。

• mpweiher高度赞扬Amiga Exec的操作系统设计，认为其通过简单的链表结构揭开了操作系统的神秘面纱。他详细描述了节点结构及其在不同系统组件（如任务、中断、消息等）中的一致性，强调了这种设计在概念上的简单性和一致性。

• vidarh强调了AmigaOS中的一些非低级API/ABI特性，如Assigns（路径别名）、Datatypes（数据类型）和Screens（虚拟桌面）。他认为这些特性在现代系统中仍然具有很高的借鉴价值，并分享了自己如何在个人项目中模拟这些特性。

• mitchbob通过引用Carl Sassenrath的贡献，表达了对AmigaOS设计者的敬意，暗示其对操作系统发展的重大影响。

• orionblastar回忆了Amiga 1000的硬件优势，指出其定制协处理器使其在性能上超越了同时期的Macintosh，并提到AROS项目可以让人在旧PC上体验Amiga的感觉。

• o11c对AmigaOS的一些被称赞的特性持怀疑态度，认为一些所谓的优点（如“无动态链接”、“无僵尸进程”）实际上是通过实现动态链接和要求程序无bug来达成的。他质疑AmigaOS与现代系统的实质区别，并认为其可靠性更多是由于较小的规模和使用门槛。

补充讨论：
• AmigaOS的链表结构和节点设计被认为是其优雅性的核心，但这也带来了安全性和现代适用性的争议。
• 不同用户对AmigaOS的特性和设计有不同的欣赏角度，从低级技术细节到高级用户功能都有涉及。
• 有人试图在现代系统中重现AmigaOS的一些特性，显示出其设计在当今仍然具有启发性和实用性。
• 对AmigaOS的历史贡献和其设计者的认可也是讨论的一部分，表明其在计算机历史中的重要地位。

RANT : Learning From the Amiga API/ABI : Zerro Below

No warranty of any kind is provided.   All information herein is provided as is without any warranty of any kind.
ASM
FUN
RANTS
WORK
CODE
Learning From the Amiga API/ABI:
The Amiga ABI is one of direct calling into shared libraries, without any run time linking at all.  This is accomplished by calling through a table of branch instructions that is at a known point in the library.  There is one library that is always at the same address, that being
Exec.library
, which includes the functions to get the addresses of the tables of other libraries.  This is an ABI that can be learned from, and can be used today even with modern memory protection.  In many ways the Amiga ABI is the ideal for applications written in C, Pascal, BCPL, Assembly Language, BASIC, etc as it does not rely on any CPU specifics and allows for any common methods of memory protection (memory protection is helpful to aid in developing software and finding bugs).
There are many things about the way that the API of Amiga OS is implemented that make for a much more usable Operating System than most are familiar with today.  These include the way that the kernel implements lists, message passing, and multitasking, the way that Intuition implements call back widgets, the way BOOPSI does not need an OO language to provide OO programming for Intuition, etc.  There has not been another OS that is as simple to program for or as well thought out as Amiga OS (and those clones that use Amiga Hunk format executable and library files).
All libraries are called by calling a negative offset from the library base address (need not be related to the image base address).  On 680x0 based systems each entry is 6 bytes, consisting of a far branch instruction (two bytes for the opcode, four for the address).  As far as I know it is 4 bytes per entry on PowerPC based systems (never had a PowerPC Amiga computer).  This is for traditional Amiga OS, now that one branch uses ELF and Dynamic linking there is a debate about which is better, in my view it is hunk without any dynamic linking needed.
Exec, the Microkernel:
At the core of the Amiga OS API is
Exec
, a Microkernel that presents itself as a library with a call table base address of 0x000004 (on 680x0 systems).  The Exec.library provides functions for memory management, task management, universal list management, starting a library (and getting the base), retrieving the base address of a loaded library, and some system management functions.  Exec knows nothing about the HW, that is left to higher level libraries.  Exec is one of the first widely successful Microkernels, and still today one of the best.
AmigaDOS and ARP:
AmigaDOS is a library that provides for the Disk and file I/O, as well as a lot of other device I/O management.  AmigaDOS also provides the standard CLI of the Amiga OS, which is fairly simple to use.
The original versions of the AmigaDOS.library were ported from the TripOS file, device, and CLI library.  This means that the early versions of AmigaDOS had an API that was heavily influenced by BCPL (the language of TripOS), and not as natural to C programmers.  Enter ARP.library (AmigaDOS Replacement Library) that provides a more natural C API for the DOS functions.  While early versions of ARP.Library were separate in Amiga OS up through 1.3, this effort became the default AmigaDOS in Amiga OS 2.0 and later.
The reason for mentioning AmigaDOS and ARP in this document is that it is one that began as a missfit though became a good fit later.  With ARP replacing much of AmigaDOS showing how dynamic the OS is do to its well thought system of libraries.
Intuition:
Many forget the amazing Windowing System that is provided by Intuition, even before BOOPSI ever came into being.  Intuition at its core is its own task that is able to call into user applications to deliver Windowing System messages, allowing a task to appropriately respond even if the primary task is temporarily zombied out.  Think about that, in modern nix systems with X or Aqua how often do you see a task go zombie and be unresponsive as a result, this was not an issue in AmigaOS do to Intuition (except with very poorly written or very poorly ported programs).
In other systems events are delivered to the program, and the main program loop has to handle them, even in preemptive multitasking systems.  This was simply not the case with Intuition, where the event handling can be completely asynchronous to the primary program.

data.title: How Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) rewrites the rules of search
data.author: eutropheon
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了生成引擎优化（GEO）如何改变搜索规则，标志着传统SEO时代的终结。随着AI语言模型（如GPT-4o、Gemini和Claude）成为信息获取的主要接口，搜索正从基于链接的系统转向基于语言理解的系统。传统SEO依赖关键词和链接提升页面排名，而GEO则注重内容质量和结构，以适应AI回答的需要。

生成引擎搜索更加个性化和多源化，答案格式变化导致搜索方式的改变。LLM市场以订阅为主，与传统搜索的广告驱动模式不同，品牌的可见性不再只依赖点击率，而是模型引用率。新平台和工具帮助品牌分析和优化在AI生成内容中的表现，监测模型如何提及和描述品牌。这使得GEO成为衡量品牌在AI时代表现的关键指标，如同传统SEO的仪表板一样重要。

主要讨论点：AI在搜索和推荐系统中的应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **AI答案的稳定性和一致性问题**：
  - [edwin] 指出AI模型的答案经常变化，即便是相同查询，Google的"AI模式"和ChatGPT只有约47%的情况下会给出相同的首条推荐。此外，ChatGPT自身的答案也会因是否依赖实时检索而不同。
  
• **AI和传统搜索的规模对比**：

How Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) Rewrites the Rules of Search
Zach Cohen
and
Seema Amble

Posted May 28, 2025
It’s the end of search as we know it, and marketers feel fine. Sort of.
For over two decades, SEO was the default playbook for visibility online. It spawned an entire industry of keyword stuffers, backlink brokers, content optimizers, and auditing tools, along with the professionals and agencies to operate them. But in 2025, search has been shifting
away
from traditional browsers toward LLM platforms. With Apple’s announcement that AI-native search engines like Perplexity and Claude will be built into Safari, Google’s distribution chokehold is
in question
. The foundation of the $80 billion+ SEO market just cracked.
A new paradigm is emerging, one driven not by page rank, but by language models. We’re entering Act II of search: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).
From links to language models
Traditional search was built on links. GEO is built on language.
In the SEO era, visibility meant ranking high on a results page. Page ranks were determined by indexing sites based on keyword matching, content depth and breadth, backlinks, user experience engagement, and more. Today, with LLMs like GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude acting as the interface for how people find information, visibility means showing up directly in the answer itself, rather than ranking high on the results page.
As the format of the answers changes, so does the way we search. AI-native search is becoming fragmented across platforms like Instagram, Amazon, and Siri, each powered by different models and user intents. Queries are
longer
(23 words, on average, vs. 4), sessions are deeper (averaging 6 minutes), and responses vary by context and source. Unlike traditional search, LLMs remember, reason, and respond with personalized, multi-source synthesis. This fundamentally changes how content is discovered and how it needs to be optimized.
Traditional SEO rewards precision and repetition; generative engines prioritize content that is well-organized, easy to parse, and dense with meaning (not just keywords). Phrases like “in summary” or bullet-point formatting help LLMs extract and reproduce content effectively
.
It’s also worth noting that the LLM market is also fundamentally different from the traditional search market in terms of business model and incentives. Classic search engines like Google monetized user traffic through ads; users paid with their data and attention. In contrast, most LLMs are paywalled, subscription-driven services. This structural shift affects how content is referenced: there’s less of an incentive by model providers to surface third-party content, unless it’s additive to the user experience or reinforces product value. While it’s possible that an ad market may eventually emerge on top of LLM interfaces, the rules, incentives, and participants would likely look very different than traditional search.
In the meantime, one emerging signal of the value in LLM interfaces is the volume of outbound clicks. ChatGPT, for instance, is already driving referral traffic to tens of thousands of distinct domains.
From rankings to model relevance
It’s no longer just about click-through rates, it’s about reference rates: how often your brand or content is cited or used as a source in model-generated answers. In a world of AI-generated outputs, GEO means optimizing for what the model
chooses
to reference, not just whether or where you appear in traditional search. That shift is revamping how we define and measure brand visibility and performance.
Already, new platforms like
Profound
,
Goodie
, and
Daydream
enable brands to analyze how they appear in AI-generated responses, track sentiment across model outputs, and understand which publishers are shaping model behavior. These platforms work by fine-tuning models to mirror brand-relevant prompt language, strategically injecting top SEO keywords, and running synthetic queries at scale. The outputs are then organized into actionable dashboards that help marketing teams monitor visibility, messaging consistency, and competitive share of voice.
Canada Goose used one such tool to gain insight into how LLMs referenced the brand — not just in terms of product features like warmth or waterproofing, but brand recognition itself. The takeaways were less about how users discovered Canada Goose, but whether the model spontaneously mentioned the brand at all, an indicator of unaided awareness in the AI era.
This kind of monitoring is becoming as important as traditional SEO dashboards. Tools like
Ahrefs
’ Brand Radar now track brand mentions in AI Overviews, helping companies understand how they’re framed and remembered by generative engines.
Semrush
also has a dedicated AI toolkit designed to help brands track perception across generative platforms, optimize content for AI vi

data.title: What works (and doesn't) selling formal methods
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: 这篇文章由Mike Dodds撰写，分享了在销售和开展形式化方法（Formal Methods, FM）项目中的经验和教训。作者强调，尽管形式化方法在过去20年里取得了增长，但在项目 scoping 和执行中仍存在许多误区。通过多次与潜在客户的交流，作者发现大多数情况下，客户并不需要或不理解形式化方法能带来的价值。客户在考虑项目时，会权衡成本与收益，只有当项目在成本效益上合理时，他们才会采纳。文章指出，许多形式化方法项目未能广泛应用，是因为它们在实际业务中无法证明自己的价值超越其他选择。因此，成功的项目必须能够明确地为客户带来实际的收益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： formal methods在软件开发中的应用、成本与收益分析

不同观点：
• agentultra认为，尽管formal methods（如模型检查）的成本常被高估，但在某些情况下，其价值不可忽视。尤其是当构建错误代价高昂时，formal methods可以通过前期投入来加速后续开发。同时，formal methods的成本和时间消耗与所追求的保证级别成正比。
• jiehong指出，formal methods的采用成本过高，90%的情况下难以被广泛接受。他认为formal methods最终应该像类型系统一样，通过编译器自动检查，并整合进CICD流程中。此外，还提到哥德尔不完备定理意味着formal methods在某些方面总会存在不足。
• Taikonerd的观点是，formal methods需要一个正式的模型，而大多数软件缺乏这种模型。比如部署软件，通常是通过大量的业务规则和错误处理来实现，而不是通过正式模型。
• stereolambda对formal methods在企业环境中的实际应用持怀疑态度，特别是对"过度类型检查"的批评，并提到在实际开发中，抽象和类型系统经常出问题。他质疑formal methods是否真的能被广泛接受，特别是考虑到人员技能和组织对新技术的接受度。
• jerf提出，formal methods的倡导者与普通开发者之间存在认知差异。普通开发者只关心程序实际运行中的状态空间，而formal methods则关注所有可能的状态空间。他认为，大多数程序在实际运行中并不会触发所有可能的状态，因此formal methods在许多情况下并不是必须的。
• freekh认为，formal methods的成本与收益分析可以应用于其他领域，比如web应用开发，视角相似。
• almostgotcaught指出，formal methods不被广泛接受的原因不仅仅是成本，而是因为需要对抽象模型达成一致，且抽象模型必须是好的系统模型。他还提到，某些证明系统虽然可以提取实现，但这些系统要求极高的精度，大多数情况下无法直接应用。
• constantcrying分享了在嵌入式航空软件开发中的经验，指出创建正式规格说明的成本非常高，且最终的功能验证无法被formal methods证明替代。他还提到团队在沟通和思维方式上的问题使得formal methods难以实施。

补充讨论：
• moi2388以幽默的方式回应了formal methods的高成本问题，暗示客户可能难以接受四倍的时间和八倍的预算。

争议焦点：
• formal methods的成本与收益是否值得，特别是与传统测试方法相比。
• formal methods的实际应用中，抽象模型的建立和团队的接受度是主要障碍。
• formal methods是否真的能解决实际开发中的问题，还是只是理论上的理想工具。

What Works (and Doesn't) Selling Formal Methods
Mike Dodds
May 8, 2025
This article began life as
a talk I gave in late 2024
.Â
I love formal methodsâI should say that to begin with, because this article is mostly about what
doesnât
work when trying to do FM projects. Over the last 20 years, formal methods have grown and grown, and Iâm proud to say that Galois has made its own contributions to this success. I made a lot of mistakes when I was scoping and running formal methods projects. Iâd like other people to avoid the pitfalls I fell into, and hopefully make bigger and more interesting mistakes.
Over my years at Galois Iâve been on a lot of sales calls. I didnât expect this - I thought I was going to work on industry applications of formal methods. But it turns out that doing research for industry requires first actually finding industry projects, and that involves
sales calls
. The result is Iâve talked to a lot of people who might, just
might
, want to do a project with Galois. Hereâs a prototypical interaction:
This kind of conversation can go two ways: either we successfully scope the project (hooray!), or we canât find a project the client wants (boo). Either case is educational, although of course the first is more satisfying. The second case is by far the majorityâmost often, we canât find a formal methods project that would help the client. Thatâs disappointing, but also, itâs
interesting
. Why is this?Â
When youâre talking to a potential client, youâre trying to figure out what they care about. Clients have real money on the line, so they care a lot about getting something they want. Quite often Iâve found that my starting intuitions are just plain wrong. Iâll say âwell, you as a person in industry <whatever> obviously want
this
â, and the client says âno we donât care about thatâ. Iâve come to realize this is
good, actually
. Having someone tell you youâre wrong really sharpens your intuitions, once you get over the bruise to your ego.Â
Over the years, Iâve formed a few opinions about what works when trying to scope formal methods projects. I certainly donât think any of these lessons are brand new, but I donât see them discussed much, and theyâre often a bit different from the conventional wisdom in formal methods research. Letâs start with the basics.Â
Worldview: Costs vs. Benefits
My basic worldview is pretty simple. Any project has expected
costs
and
benefits
. Thereâs some client-specific break-even line above which a given project makes sense. Below that line, the project is too costly, and itâs not worth doing.Â Â
Here Iâm thinking about
holistic
cost: time, money, people, resources â anything that requires something of your organization; and holistic benefit â security, reliability, economic value, happiness, being able to sleep at night, all those kinds of things. And of course, the break-even line isnât straight but is probably some fancy multi-dimensional surface. This is a
highly abstract and very inaccurate model of the world
. But in some sense, it reflects how we make decisions in everyday life. Something cheap and very beneficial is probably something you should do, and something expensive and not very beneficial is probably something you should not do.
Potential clients of formal methods are somewhat rational when it comes to costs and benefits. They know what's high priority and low priority. They have a limited budget for projects, and they weigh projects against each other. Projects that make sense to clients in terms of cost-benefit tradeoffs will happen, and projects that donât, wonât happen.Â
This seems almost trivial - how does it help? Well, I also see a lot of confusion about why formal methods arenât adopted more widely. I think the explanation is actually quite simple.
Many potential formal methods projects donât make sense in terms of cost/benefit tradeoffs
.Â
Sometimes in formal method research, we talk about whatâs
possible
. For example, we now have great projects like
SeL4
,
CompCert
, and
HACL
Â  that show itâs
possible
to create industrially-useful systems with formal guarantees. Thatâs a great accomplishment, but all of those projects were funded as research efforts. If we want more formally verified projects, those projects have to not just be possible, but also be more valuable to clients than other things they could do with their resources.Â
Iâm going to give a few specific takes about scoping formal methods projects. But my core claim is that projects have to make sense in terms of costs and benefits. Thatâs all.Â
1: Projects Have to Deliver Value

data.title: How can AI researchers save energy? By going backward
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能研究中如何通过可逆计算节省能源。传统计算机在删除数据时会产生热量，造成能量损失，这是由物理学家罗夫·兰道尔在1960年代提出的理论。迈克尔·弗兰克等研究者探索了可逆计算，即通过不删除数据来避免这种能量损失。可逆程序既能向前也能向后运行，从而在理论上节省能源。尽管早期认为可逆计算不切实际，但查尔斯·班纳特在1973年提出了“非计算”概念，通过运行计算后存储结果并反向运行，以节省能量并保留必要数据。随着传统计算遇到物理极限，可逆计算有望在人工智能领域发挥重要作用，可能显著提升计算效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于可逆计算及其潜在应用、技术可行性和能源效率的讨论

不同观点：
• [rollcat] 认为现代技术的外部成本被忽视，技术带来的效率提升通常被用于获取更多利益，而不是减少对他人的伤害。他提到可逆计算可能有助于减少对环境的负面影响。
• [imurray] 对可逆计算的能源动机持怀疑态度，但承认其在深度学习架构中的潜在应用。他指出，尽管理论上可逆计算是可行的，但由于舍入误差等实际问题，完全可逆在实践中很难实现。
• [tamat] 作为一名软件工程师，他对可逆计算的概念感到困惑。他质疑所有逻辑门操作是否都会导致电子损失，以及保存所有内存变化历史如何能防止热量损失，并询问这种技术的实际用途。
• [user____name] 提到Jevons悖论，认为即使可逆计算技术出现，也可能不会显著减少能源消耗，因为新技术的效率提升往往导致更多的使用。
• [MangoToupe] 对计算的方向性提出疑问，并询问可逆计算是否仅仅是通过默认保存状态来实现回溯。
• [worldsayshi] 提到Mike P Frank对可逆计算和人工智能的研究，暗示Frank可能对这一领域有深入见解。
• [thrance] 引用科幻小说《时间》中的情节，描述了在宇宙热寂状态下，可逆计算可能成为唯一的计算方式，尽管这是一个极端的假设场景。
• [throwawaymaths] 质疑是否有人已经实现了可逆计算的矩阵乘法运算，并指出在这种转换的边缘仍然会有信息损失。
• [sadboots] 提到使用大语言模型所需的电力比烧水还少，暗示现有技术在能源效率上可能已经有所进步。
• [charcircuit] 对文章缺乏基准和证据支持表示失望，质疑可逆计算技术在实际性能上能否与传统芯片竞争。
• [Huxley1] 表示对可逆计算的新奇和兴趣，认为这种技术可能在节省能源方面有潜力，并计划进一步了解。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于可逆计算在实际应用中的可行性和其是否真能显著减少能源消耗。
• 不同的技术细节和实现难题也被广泛讨论，比如计算的可逆性在实际操作中的舍入误差问题。
• 有人对可逆计算的实际应用场景表示质疑，认为缺乏明确的用途和竞争优势。
• 讨论中也涉及到科幻文学中的极端假设，作为对未来技术发展的一种展望。

How Can AI Researchers Save Energy? By Going Backward.
By
Matt von Hippel
May 30, 2025
Reversible programs run backward as easily as they run forward, saving energy in theory. After decades of research, they may soon power AI.

or Michael Frank, efficiency has always been a major preoccupation. As a student in the 1990s, he was originally interested in artificial intelligence. But once he realized how much energy the technology would use, he took his research in another direction. “I started getting interested in the physical limits of computation,” he said. “What’s the most efficient computer you can possibly build?”
He soon found a candidate that took advantage of a quirk of thermodynamics: a device whose computations could run backward as well as forward. By never deleting data, such a “reversible” computer would avoid wasted energy.
Now, as progress in traditional computing is slowing — new chips are running into
fundamental physical limitations
that prevent them from getting smaller — reversible computing could keep computational progress going.
“There aren’t that many other ways to improve power,” said
Christof Teuscher
, who researches unconventional approaches to computing at Portland State University. “Reversible computing is this really beneficial, really exciting way of saving potentially orders of magnitude.”
Feeling the Heat
The first person to study reversible computing was Rolf Landauer, a celebrated physicist at IBM who in the 1960s helped establish the field of information processing. A major theme in his work involved the relationship between
entropy, which is a measure of disorder
, and information.
Roughly speaking, the more we know about a system the more orderly its arrangement can be, and the less we know, the less orderly. Atoms going from predictable behavior to unpredictable motion is what makes some physical processes irreversible. For example, when you stir milk into coffee, disorder increases. You can, in theory, separate them again to make the arrangement of milk molecules and coffee molecules more orderly. But to do so, you’d need knowledge of the path of each drop of milk, an implausibly vast amount of information.
In 1961, Landauer
showed
that these principles govern computers as well. When a computer system deletes information, electrons in the computer’s chips go from known paths to unknown ones. Those discarded electrons are effectively lost, and their energy bleeds off as heat. Landauer proved that this is an inescapable fact: No matter how a computer is built, it must give off a certain minimum amount of heat for each bit of information it deletes.

Michael Frank has long worked to make practical reversible computers, which would save considerable energy by not deleting data.
Johnny Carroll/Albuquerque Headshot & Portrait
This loss is a fundamental aspect of how computers operate. For example, when a computer adds two numbers together, it returns a single number for the total: 2 + 2 = 4. There’s a loss of information as you go from two numbers to one. You could have added 2 and 2, or you could have combined 1 and 3. The missing information makes the calculation irreversible. Computers that process information this way — and almost all of them do — are always going to lose some information as heat, no matter what.
Landauer wondered if a machine could get around this limitation by simply never deleting data. Such a device would need to keep a record of every operation, every pair of numbers added at every step. These records would rapidly fill its memory, making such a computer unusable in practice, despite the energy savings. Landauer soon moved on, convinced that reversible computing was a dead end.
A decade later, he learned that he had been mistaken.
Hitting Reverse
Charles Bennett, a younger colleague of Landauer’s at IBM,
argued
in 1973 that there was another option. Instead of saving every single scrap of information, you could run each calculation forward, store the result you care about, then run the calculation backward. Bennett’s idea, which he called uncomputation, is a little like if Hansel and Gretel picked up their trail of breadcrumbs on the way back home: The pair are guaranteed not to get lost, and they don’t waste any breadcrumbs. data.title: TPDE: A Fast Adaptable Compiler Back-End Framework
data.author: npalli
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为TPDE的编译器后端框架，旨在加速即时编译（JIT）过程中的代码生成。与LLVM等传统框架不同，TPDE无需额外的中间表示（IR）转换步骤，能够直接适应现有SSA形式的代码表示，从而减少延迟。通过一次分析和一次编译过程，TPDE结合了指令选择、寄存器分配和指令编码。实验显示，TPDE在SPECint 2017基准测试中编译LLVM-IR的速度比LLVM -O0快8到24倍，且运行时性能相当。此外，TPDE在WebAssembly和数据库查询编译等特定领域IR中展现了降低编译延迟的优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于LLVM和TPDE项目的构建、功能、性能以及其在LLVM生态中的定位

不同观点：
• MaskRay提供了详细的构建指令，并指出了在构建和测试过程中遇到的一些失败测试，具体列出了失败的测试案例，如`codegen/eh-frame-eh64.tir`等。这表明该项目在某些测试上存在问题，仍需改进。
• npalli提供了TPDE框架的源代码链接，为其他讨论者提供了进一步了解和研究该项目的基础。
• BarakWidawsky提出了关于TPDE项目定位的问题，询问它是否会取代Cranelift，暗示了对该项目功能定位的疑惑以及与Cranelift潜在的功能重叠。
• fooker质疑项目被描述为“可适应的”和“框架”的原因，认为这些术语可能是噱头，并强调其作为一个LLVM后端的实用性。
• xiphias2认为该项目虽然起步不错，但真正的挑战在于将其整合为LLVM默认的`-O0`编译器，指出这部分工作的必要性和难度。
• vlovich123对项目的性能声称表示惊讶，特别是其编译速度比LLVM的`-O0`快8-24倍，同时运行时性能与`-O3`相当，质疑其真实性或实现方式。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对项目定位、性能声称以及术语使用的质疑，尤其是与现有工具（如Cranelift）的比较和潜在竞争关系。
• 构建和测试过程中遇到的具体问题（如失败测试）为项目的改进提供了方向。
• 讨论还涉及到将项目整合到LLVM中的技术挑战和未来发展方向。

Title:
TPDE: A Fast Adaptable Compiler Back-End Framework
Authors:
Tobias Schwarz
(1),
Tobias Kamm
(1),
Alexis Engelke
(1) ((1) Technical University of Munich)
View a PDF of the paper titled TPDE: A Fast Adaptable Compiler Back-End Framework, by Tobias Schwarz (1) and 2 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Fast machine code generation is especially important for fast start-up just-in-time compilation, where the compilation time is part of the end-to-end latency. However, widely used compiler frameworks like LLVM do not prioritize fast compilation and require an extra IR translation step increasing latency even further; and rolling a custom code generator is a substantial engineering effort, especially when targeting multiple architectures.
Therefore, in this paper, we present TPDE, a compiler back-end framework that adapts to existing code representations in SSA form. Using an IR-specific adapter providing canonical access to IR data structures and a specification of the IR semantics, the framework performs one analysis pass and then performs the compilation in just a single pass, combining instruction selection, register allocation, and instruction encoding. The generated target instructions are primarily derived code written in high-level language through LLVM's Machine IR, easing portability to different architectures while enabling optimizations during code generation.
To show the generality of our framework, we build a new back-end for LLVM from scratch targeting x86-64 and AArch64. Performance results on SPECint 2017 show that we can compile LLVM-IR 8--24x faster than LLVM -O0 while being on-par in terms of run-time performance. We also demonstrate the benefits of adapting to domain-specific IRs in JIT contexts, particularly WebAssembly and database query compilation, where avoiding the extra IR translation further reduces compilation latency.

data.title: The Princeton INTERCAL Compiler's source code
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
《Forty-Four Esolangs》一书将于2025年9月23日发布，首次公开了普林斯顿INTERCAL编译器的源代码。INTERCAL由唐·伍兹和吉姆·里昂于1972年在普林斯顿大学创作，是第一个被称为“esolang”的编程语言，故意颠覆传统编程规则，以符号和独特设计（如“#”代表“mesh”）挑战程序员。该语言最具特色的功能是“PLEASE”命令，使用过多或过少都会导致程序被忽略，模仿了人类与算法之间的模糊关系。

尽管INTERCAL-72编译器从未广泛传播，但其影响深远，启发了如Chicken、Ook!等语言。最著名的“COME FROM”语句则是1990年由Eric S. Raymond添加的。通过最新技术，现在可以首次体验原版INTERCAL-72编译器，了解其独特的数学运算方式。

44155247.article_content:
New Book, out Sept 23, 2025:
Forty-Four Esolangs
, the first artist's monograph of programming language concepts.
Published for the first time: the Princeton INTERCAL Compiler's source code
It is with great excitement that we share the original INTERCAL-72 compiler source code, as both scans and transcriptions (see below). INTERCAL was created by Don Woods (
previously interviewed here
) and Jim Lyon as undergrads at Princeton in an infamous late-night session after freshman finals in 1972. Don recently rediscovered a print-out, on green-barred, continuous-feed pages, of the SPITBOL source code for the original compiler. If the legend holds true, this code had not been run since Woods and Lyon's Princeton days. Sean Haas (of the
Advent of Computing
podcast) and I transcribed the code from these scans, proof-reading each others' interpretations of fading characters. Haas has also produced a refined, runnable version of the script.
INTERCAL ("Compiler Language with No Pronounceable Acronym") is the first language that can unequivocally be called an esolang. While previous languages had odd designs as pl research and experimentation, INTERCAL intentionally subverts its programmers' effort to write what Dijkstra called "good code": that which "shortens the conceptual gap between the static program and the dynamic process." In INTERCAL, code is circuitous, full of symbols used in bizarre ways and with unique designations (#, for example, is the "mesh" sign). It is a challenge to read or to run in ones head, even for those deeply immersed in the language. Furthermore, it does this for parody and play, not with any practical aim in mind.
The length of INTERCAL's shadow cannot be overstated. It was twenty years after its creation that a series of minimalist languages (FALSE, Befunge, brainfuck) took the next steps toward what would become the esolang movement. INTERCAL-72 offered somewhat of a different path from these; it was less concerned with minimalism, and more explicitly dramatized the act of programming. Woods and Lyon described it as eschewing conventions of languages like ALGOL, SNOBOL, FOCAL, and AP/I, yet it is also clearly parody, embracing and exaggerating their worst eccentricities and inefficiencies for an alienating experience.
INTERCAL's most striking feature is its humanizing of the interpreter, a mercurial being who we literally plead with to get our programs to run. Use the command PLEASE too little and the interpreter will be offended and ignore the whole program; use it too much and it writes you off as a suck-up and... also ignore the whole program. Its subjectivity feels particularly relevant in an age when AI systems are designed to deliberately confuse the human and algorithmic. The influence of just this one feature can be seen in early parody languages like Chicken and Ook! that undermine the seriousness of the interpreter, to
English
, where the interpreter was once literally another person but is now downgraded to an AI prompt system. More personally, the interpreter for my
language Olympus
has many, competing personalities in the form of the Greek gods, any of which might become offended and ignore the rest of the program, in INTERCAL style.
However, for such an influential esolang, it is one that we experience primarily in derivative forms. The most well-known INTERCAL keyword (apart from PLEASE) is not part of the INTERCAL-72 language at all. That would be the COME FROM statement, an inverse of GOTO, where one has to trace back jumps from destination to source, like cheating in a choose-your-own-adventure book. It was added in 1990 by Eric S Raymond (
interviewed here
) for his adaptation C-INTERCAL. The original INTERCAL-72 compiler never left Princeton according to Woods; it is likely that ESR worked from the INTERCAL-72 manual without access to the reference compiler. Almost all who have used the language since then have actually used C-INTERCAL or one of its successors (CLC-INTERCAL etc). These later versions capture much of the spirit of the original but differ significantly in style and content. Now, with access to the original, we can experience INTERCAL-72 first-hand and make new discoveries.
Sean Haas describes the process of getting the ical.sbl (INTERCAL compiler) program running on a modern system, using SPITBOLx64. As he points out, ICAL is actually a transpiler; some of its infamous slowness is due to the overhead of generating a SPITBOL program and executing it. More surprisingly, it avoids SPITBOL's math functions, performing math through pure string manipulation. Sean discusses this in
the latest episode
of his podcast, Advent of Code, explaining the infamous thirty seconds needed to perform a single division:
The two operations you get, called MINGLE and SELECT, operate on binary data. Internally, ICAL will store numbers as a string of binary digits. A 4 becomes "100", for instance. When you operate on that number it's done as a string operation. The result is tha

《Forty-Four Esolangs》一书将于2025年9月23日发布，首次公开了普林斯顿INTERCAL编译器的源代码。INTERCAL由唐·伍兹和吉姆·里昂于1972年在普林斯顿大学创作，是第一个被称为“esolang”的编程语言，故意颠覆传统编程规则，以符号和独特设计（如“#”代表“mesh”）挑战程序员。该语言最具特色的功能是“PLEASE”命令，使用过多或过少都会导致程序被忽略，模仿了人类与算法之间的模糊关系。

data.author: Daril
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HeidiSQL的使用体验、跨平台可用性、与同类工具的比较以及其技术实现和未来发展方向

不同观点：
• **支持与赞赏**：一些用户对HeidiSQL表示强烈支持，认为它是最好的桌面SQL工具之一，特别赞赏其简洁、高效以及长期以来的改进（如[atmanactive]，[devgoncalo]，[sakesun]）。
  
• **对Bug和稳定性的批评**：部分用户提到HeidiSQL存在一些稳定性问题，如UI锁定、异常弹窗等（如[rorylaitila]，[deergomoo]，[Grazester]）。这些用户虽然使用HeidiSQL，但也指出了其不足之处，有些人因此转向了其他工具如DBeaver。

• **跨平台需求的满足**：一些用户对HeidiSQL推出Linux版本表示欢迎，特别是之前需要通过Wine在Linux上使用HeidiSQL的用户（如[spapas82]，[rd07]，[Shorel]）。同时，也有用户关注HeidiSQL与其他跨平台工具如DbGate的比较（如[sandreas]，[moron4hire]）。

• **与其他工具的比较**：一些用户将HeidiSQL与DBeaver、DataGrip等工具进行对比，指出HeidiSQL的优势（如简洁、高效）和不足（如对某些数据库的支持不够完善）。部分用户提到如果需要处理更复杂的任务，他们会选择功能更强大的工具如MS SQL管理工具或DataGrip（如[redditor98654]，[Grazester]，[moron4hire]）。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现与未来发展**：有用户关注HeidiSQL的技术实现，特别是从Delphi到FreePascal/Lazarus的移植过程，提到了一些技术上的挑战和未来可能的发展方向，如SQL方言的抽象化（如[igitur]）。
  
• **社区贡献的呼吁**：一些用户呼吁社区对HeidiSQL进行财务或代码上的支持，认为这是推动项目发展的重要方式（如[igitur]）。

总体来看，用户对HeidiSQL的评价褒贬不一，主要争议点在于其稳定性和功能完善度，而其简洁和高效则是用户持续使用的重要原因。同时，HeidiSQL推出Linux版本受到了广泛欢迎，用户对其未来发展也寄予了一些期望。

data.title: Show HN: Moon Phase Algorithms for C, Lua, Awk, JavaScript, etc.
data.author: oliverkwebb
data.article_summary: 该项目收集了用于计算当前月相的代码片段，支持多种编程语言和领域特定语言（DSL），包括C、Rust、Zig、JavaScript、Python、Lua、awk和bc。这些函数接受时间输入，返回月相的"年龄"（以弧度表示），进而计算月球的照明比例和百分比。通过将月相年龄映射到[0,1]范围，再乘以约29.5，可得到以天为单位的月相年龄。项目还提供了计算月相"索引"的示例（如Rust代码所示），用于获取月相名称和表情符号。所有代码均基于20世纪80年代John Walker的Moontool程序算法，并遵循0BSD许可证。代码要求自包含且尽可能纯净，避免影响外部环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：月亮 phase 计算程序及其相关技术细节和实现方法

不同观点：
• **kbr2000** 分享了一个用于可视化月亮 phase 的 PostScript 程序，并提到该程序可以生成未来十年的月亮 phase 图像，适应特定框架。这表明该程序不仅功能性强，还具有实用性和美观性。
• **rybosome** 对代码的纯函数要求发表看法，认为这种限制对于编程风格有影响，尤其是对环境的最小影响要求，需要对语言运行时有较深入的理解。这反映出在实现算法时，保持代码的独立性和纯净度具有挑战性。
• **blululu** 提到简单地将时间间隔除以月亮的 synodic 周期来计算 phase 的想法，并指出这种方法的不准确性，强调了月亮 phase 计算的复杂性，提供了维基百科链接以供参考。
• **o11c** 提到 `pom(6)` 程序可能已经存在于系统中用于类似目的，并推荐了 Rosetta Code 作为实现多语言简单任务的资源。这表明在选择工具和资源时，已有解决方案可能被忽视。
• **librasteve** 提交了一个 Raku 语言的 PR，并分享了代码中的亮点，包括使用 Raku 特有的语法和函数来处理数学计算，展示了 Raku 在处理复杂计算时的优势。
• **lifthrasiir** 对角度归一化方法提出改进建议，认为将角度转换到 [0, 360) 范围是多余的，建议使用 [0, 2) 范围以提高计算精度和效率，这表明在数学计算中选择合适的归一化方法至关重要。
• **ericpruitt** 提到将月亮 phase 逻辑适配到状态栏程序中，并提出了在处理日期转换时遇到的差异问题，提供了具体代码链接以供参考。
• **anthk** 简短提到 AWK 的强大功能，暗示其在领域特定语言（DSL）之外的广泛应用潜力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于计算月亮 phase 的复杂性及其不同实现方法的准确性。blululu 强调了简单方法的不足，而 ericpruitt 则具体指出了日期转换中的实际问题。
• 讨论中多次提到不同编程语言和工具的实现方法，包括 Raku 和 AWK，展示了多语言解决方案在处理特定问题时的多样性和灵活性。
• 技术细节如角度归一化、纯函数要求和数学函数的应用，展示了在实现月亮 phase 计算时需要考虑的多个技术层面。

moonphase - Werewolf Early Warning System
A collection of snippets that get the phase of the moon, currently, the implementations are:
Systems Level Languages:
C/C++
Rust
Zig
Scripting Languages:
Lua

(1-cos(x))/2

主要讨论点：月亮 phase 计算程序及其相关技术细节和实现方法

不同观点：
• **kbr2000** 分享了一个用于可视化月亮 phase 的 PostScript 程序，并提到该程序可以生成未来十年的月亮 phase 图像，适应特定框架。这表明该程序不仅功能性强，还具有实用性和美观性。
• **rybosome** 对代码的纯函数要求发表看法，认为这种限制对于编程风格有影响，尤其是对环境的最小影响要求，需要对语言运行时有较深入的理解。这反映出在实现算法时，保持代码的独立性和纯净度具有挑战性。
• **blululu** 提到简单地将时间间隔除以月亮的 synodic 周期来计算 phase 的想法，并指出这种方法的不准确性，强调了月亮 phase 计算的复杂性，提供了维基百科链接以供参考。
• **o11c** 提到 `pom(6)` 程序可能已经存在于系统中用于类似目的，并推荐了 Rosetta Code 作为实现多语言简单任务的资源。这表明在选择工具和资源时，已有解决方案可能被忽视。
• **librasteve** 提交了一个 Raku 语言的 PR，并分享了代码中的亮点，包括使用 Raku 特有的语法和函数来处理数学计算，展示了 Raku 在处理复杂计算时的优势。
• **lifthrasiir** 对角度归一化方法提出改进建议，认为将角度转换到 [0, 360) 范围是多余的，建议使用 [0, 2) 范围以提高计算精度和效率，这表明在数学计算中选择合适的归一化方法至关重要。
• **ericpruitt** 提到将月亮 phase 逻辑适配到状态栏程序中，并提出了在处理日期转换时遇到的差异问题，提供了具体代码链接以供参考。
• **anthk** 简短提到 AWK 的强大功能，暗示其在领域特定语言（DSL）之外的广泛应用潜力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于计算月亮 phase 的复杂性及其不同实现方法的准确性。blululu 强调了简单方法的不足，而 ericpruitt 则具体指出了日期转换中的实际问题。
• 讨论中多次提到不同编程语言和工具的实现方法，包括 Raku 和 AWK，展示了多语言解决方案在处理特定问题时的多样性和灵活性。
• 技术细节如角度归一化、纯函数要求和数学函数的应用，展示了在实现月亮 phase 计算时需要考虑的多个技术层面。

data.title: LFSR CPU Running Forth
data.author: izabera
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了使用线性反馈移位寄存器（LFSR）作为程序计数器的CPU实现，该项目基于VHDL语言，面向FPGA。与传统程序计数器相比，LFSR可以节省逻辑门数量，特别适用于7400系列IC或手动布局晶体管的场景。项目包含一个完整的Forth解释器，目前在仿真中运行成功，输出启动消息"eForth 3.3"并接受输入。该CPU资源占用小，运行频率可达151.768MHz，使用少量FPGA资源。项目提供构建指南，通过GHDL进行仿真，使用Xilinx ISE 14.7进行FPGA合成。CPU为累加器架构，指令长度16位，程序计数器由8位LFSR驱动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LFSR-PC（线性反馈移位寄存器程序计数器）在处理器设计中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• howerj认为，LFSR-PC是一个非常小众的处理器，实际应用价值不大。他完成这个项目主要是为了探索可能性，并借机宣传自己的求职信息。
• tyrellj表示，自己在探索LFSR及相关概念（如Subleq和OISC）时感到困惑，尤其是之前未听说过LFSR，并对未选修更多硬件/电子课程感到遗憾。
• jsd1982提出疑问，LFSR-PC是否会给汇编器/编译器在发出带有目标PC偏移的分支指令时带来挑战，例如计算相距两条指令的偏移量时是否会产生错误。
• kragen指出，LFSR-PC的概念在1970年代的TMS 1000等处理器中已有应用，并详细讨论了LFSR-PC在跳转指令中的潜在优势和问题，如避免地址字段和可能需要插入NOP指令。他还提到TMS 1000的页面地址寄存器设计以节省空间。
• artemonster分享了自己在继电器CPU中使用LFSR-PC技巧的经验，通过使用3个继电器实现12位增量，而非24个继电器，从而简化了设计。
• nullc认为，LFSR-PC这样的优化可能在追求最低能量消耗的CPU设计中出现，但许多有趣的低能量优化涉及模拟/晶体管层面，超出了业余爱好者的能力范围。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体例子包括TMS 1000、Atari 2600的TIA、UM66T音乐芯片和Pentium自检电路中LFSR的应用。
• kragen和artemonster提供了实际项目中的技术细节和实现方法，展示了LFSR-PC在不同硬件环境中的可行性和优势。
• nullc指出了LFSR优化在能量效率方面的潜力，但也强调了其复杂性和专业性，限制了业余爱好者的参与。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于LFSR-PC的实际应用价值。howerj认为其应用价值不大，而kragen和artemonster通过具体例子展示了其在特定场景中的优势。

LFSR CPU running Forth
Author: Richard James Howe
License: 0BSD / Public Domain
Email:
mailto:howe.r.j.89@gmail.com
Repo:
https://github.com/howerj/lfsr-vhdl
This project contains a CPU written in
VHDL
for an
FPGA
using a Linear Feedback Shift
Register (
LFSR
) instead of a Program Counter, this was sometimes done to save space as
a
LFSR
requires fewer gates than an adder, however on an FPGA it will make very
little difference as the units that make an FPGA (Slices/Configurable Logic
Blocks) have carry chains in them. The saving would perhaps be more apparent if
making the system out of
7400
series ICs, or if laying transistors out by hand.
See
https://github.com/howerj/lfsr
for more information.
The system contains a fully working
Forth
interpreter.
The project currently works in simulation (it outputs the startup message
"eForth 3.3" with a new line) and accepts input (try typing "words" when the
simulation in
GHDL
is running).
Here is an example session of the simulator running:
And the VHDL running under GHDL for a limited number of cycles:
CPU Resource Utilization
The system runs can run at 151.768MHz (on a Spartan-6) according to the timing
report. The CPU itself is quite small, here is a cut-down report on the
resources consumed for commit
7dc4c9b7e03082364b09540bb2d97105d2858d0b
:
+------------------------------------------------------------+
| Module     | Slices | Slice Reg | LUTs  | BRAM/FIFO | BUFG |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
| top/       | 3/53   | 9/105     | 1/151 | 0/8       | 1/1  |
| +system    | 0/27   | 0/47      | 0/85  | 0/8       | 0/0  |
| ++bram     | 0/0    | 0/0       | 0/0   | 8/8       | 0/0  |
| ++cpu      | 27/27  | 47/47     | 85/85 | 0/0       | 0/0  |
| +uart_rx_0 | 12/12  | 24/24     | 39/39 | 0/0       | 0/0  |
| +uart_tx_0 | 11/11  | 25/25     | 26/26 | 0/0       | 0/0  |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
No LUTRAM/BUFIO/DSP48A1/BUFR/DCM/PLL_ADV used
The above is indicative only as the actual resources used may vary from
commit to commit, but also because of the tool chain and FPGA targeted.
Even given that though it is clear that this system is
small
. The CPU
only occupies 27 slices, which is only a little larger than the bit-serial
CPU available at
https://github.com/howerj/bit-serial
, and this 16-bit CPU
is
much
faster.
Building
To build you will need
make
. To make the C Virtual Machine you will need a C
compiler of your choosing.
To run the C VM type:
make run
You should be greeted by the message
eforth 3.3
. Type
bye
and hit
ENTER
to quit (
CTRL-D
will not work, this is not a bug). Type
words
for a list of
defined Forth words. An example session:
: ahoy cr ." GOODBYE, CRUEL WORLD!" cr ;
ahoy
2 2 + . cr
bye
This is not a Forth tutorial. For a Forth tutorial look elsewhere. Try "the
internet". I am sure they have something.
Making the simulation requires
GHDL
:
make simulation
There is a configuration file for the simulation in the file
tb.cfg
that
allows changing many test bench parameters without recompiling the test bench.
GHDL also allows you to set generics via the command line, which is done in the
makefile
. For example
make simulation DEBUG=2
sets the top level debug
generic to
2
, bear in mind when changing the generics in
tb.vhd
that the
makefile
can override these constants!
To build for an FPGA you will need
Xilinx ISE 14.7
:
make synthesis implementation bitfile
The system has not been tested on an FPGA at the moment. If you have any luck,
let me know.
Instruction Set and System Design
A short summary of the instruction set and design:
The machine is an accumulator based machine.
All instructions are 16-bits in length.
The top four bits determine the instruction.
The lowest four bits are the operand parameter.
Addresses are in number of 16-bit cells, not bytes.
The program counter is 8-bits in size and is advanced with a LFSR.
The top most bit determined whether the operand is used directly or
whether or it loaded first.
The instruction set has been carefully chosen so that it
should be very simple to implement in a

data.title: Is “The Phoenician Scheme” Wes Anderson's Most Emotional Film?
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary:
韦斯·安德森的新片《腓尼基方案》是一部充满幽默的喜剧，但故事本身却颇为沉重，讲述了一个富有实业家试图实现宏大基建项目的过程。影片延续了安德森标志性的精致布景、对称构图和紧凑复杂的情节，同时也是一部充满打斗和追逐的暴力电影。与《布达佩斯大饭店》及之后作品的嵌套叙事不同，本片情节相对简单，集中跟随主角的行动。

故事聚焦于一个有趣但恶劣的男人安托瓦内·科尔达（本尼西奥·德尔·托罗饰），他是一位毫无顾忌的商业巨头。在1950年至1951年间，他试图推动一个涉及运河、隧道、铁路和水库的腓尼基国家项目，不惜使用奴隶劳工。尽管面临美国特工、国际财团和革命者的威胁，他依然冷酷无情。

影片通过科尔达与女儿利瑟尔（米娅·瑟普莱顿饰）及同父异母兄弟努巴（本尼迪克特·康伯巴奇饰）的关系，展现了家庭内部的复杂情感。安德森以精美的设计和情感张力，讲述了一个无情商人为了赢得虔诚女儿的爱而不惜一切的悲剧故事。

Wes Anderson’s new film, “The Phoenician Scheme,” is a funny-ha-ha comedy, but there’s nothing funny about its story, which involves a wealthy industrialist’s attempts to realize a grandiose infrastructure project. Anderson’s signature is instantly recognizable in the movie’s decorative production design, its frontal and symmetrical framings, and its antic, densely plotted story—and equally in the fact that it is a violent and death-haunted action film, filled with fights and chases. Yet, compared with “The Grand Budapest Hotel” (2014) and the work that has followed, the new film is relatively simple: rather than nesting stories within other stories, it follows its protagonist closely. The result is a heightened clarity—revealing the distinctive world view that Anderson’s methods embody—and an unusually direct emotionalism.
“The Phoenician Scheme” is the story of an amusingly bad man who becomes a little less amusing and a little less bad. Benicio del Toro, alternately glowering and glib, stars as Anatole (Zsa-zsa) Korda, an Onassis-like figure of uninhibited ruthlessness. The action, which runs from 1950 to late 1951, begins as Zsa-zsa, a proud citizen of no country, flits about in a private Air Korda plane that he knows to be a target of saboteurs. Sure enough, mid-flight, a hole is blown in the fuselage, and Zsa-zsa, taking the controls, crash-lands the plane. Unconscious, he has a near-death experience—filmed in black-and-white with a sense of both comedy and wonderment—in which he arrives in a cotton-puff Heaven under the severe scrutiny of a berobed gatekeeper (played by Willem Dafoe).
Badly wounded, Zsa-zsa recuperates in his sixteenth-century Italian palazzo, and summons his twenty-year-old daughter, Liesl (Mia Threapleton), a novitiate nun. She’s the eldest of his ten children (the other nine are boys), and he wants her to renounce her vocation and become the heir to his enterprises, at a critical moment. A grand project in the fictitious country of Phoenicia, thirty years in the making—involving a canal, a tunnel, a railroad line, and a dam—may finally be coming to fruition, and Zsa-zsa, who is set to get five per cent of the profits, will stop at nothing to realize it. The film sardonically conjures a golden age of interventionist arrogance. Though there’s no explicit mention of the Cold War, there’s plenty of espionage and intrigue. Zsa-zsa’s many enemies include American secret agents, an international business consortium, and a well-armed band of revolutionaries, led by a man named Sergio (Richard Ayoade). Zsa-zsa’s scheme comes at a high human cost: it may bring modernization to Phoenicia, but it will depend on slave labor. This doesn’t trouble his conscience any more than does his reputation for financial misdeeds. But the scheme puts several targets on his back: governments and corporate entities see him as a loose cannon, and the revolutionaries see him as a predator.
It’s no wonder that Zsa-zsa is accustomed to assassination attempts. At meals, he puts a drop of reagent into his drinks, and he is unruffled when one turns out to be poisoned. He is at home with violence, literally: he keeps a box full of hand grenades nearby at all times and offers them to guests as if they were cigars or chocolates. He endures danger, such as a submersion in quicksand, with gruff equanimity. He also keeps his cool in heated dealings with a far-flung cast of associates whose backing he needs: with Prince Farouk (Riz Ahmed), he faces two Americans (Tom Hanks and Bryan Cranston) in a high-stakes basketball shoot-out; he takes a bullet for Marseille Bob (Mathieu Amalric) in the Frenchman’s Art Deco night club; he negotiates with the Newark Syndicate’s hipster representative, Marty (Jeffrey Wright), with the aid of deadly force. Closer to home, he hopes to marry a rich second cousin, Hilda Sussman-Korda (Scarlett Johansson), and seeks the support of an estranged half brother, called Uncle Nubar (Benedict Cumberbatch).
This last relationship becomes particularly fraught. Zsa-zsa has outlived all three of his wives, including Liesl’s mother, and Liesl has heard rumors that he killed her, or had her killed. When she confronts him, he pins the blame on Nubar, and Liesl demands that her uncle be punished. (Threapleton, in her first major feature-film role, has a striking presence, both quietly fierce and effortlessly wry.) Thus the movie’s financial and martial machinations take place within a more elemental family drama: in order to win his daughter’s allegiance and affection, Zsa-zsa must pursue a mock-Shakespearean plot of fratricidal revenge. “The Phoenician Scheme” is Anderson’s most sentimental movie—the story of a merciless man so desperate for his devout daughter’s love that he’s willing to kill for it.

韦斯·安德森的新片《腓尼基方案》是一部充满幽默的喜剧，但故事本身却颇为沉重，讲述了一个富有实业家试图实现宏大基建项目的过程。影片延续了安德森标志性的精致布景、对称构图和紧凑复杂的情节，同时也是一部充满打斗和追逐的暴力电影。与《布达佩斯大饭店》及之后作品的嵌套叙事不同，本片情节相对简单，集中跟随主角的行动。

故事聚焦于一个有趣但恶劣的男人安托瓦内·科尔达（本尼西奥·德尔·托罗饰），他是一位毫无顾忌的商业巨头。在1950年至1951年间，他试图推动一个涉及运河、隧道、铁路和水库的腓尼基国家项目，不惜使用奴隶劳工。尽管面临美国特工、国际财团和革命者的威胁，他依然冷酷无情。

影片通过科尔达与女儿利瑟尔（米娅·瑟普莱顿饰）及同父异母兄弟努巴（本尼迪克特·康伯巴奇饰）的关系，展现了家庭内部的复杂情感。安德森以精美的设计和情感张力，讲述了一个无情商人为了赢得虔诚女儿的爱而不惜一切的悲剧故事。

data.title: In POSIX, you can theoretically use inode zero
data.author: mfrw
data.article_summary: 本文是博客作者Chris Siebenmann对使用旧浏览器访问其博客或wiki系统CSpace时被误拦截的说明。由于2025年初高流量爬虫（包括用于LLM训练的数据爬虫）大量使用旧浏览器用户代理（尤其是Chrome），作者为减轻服务器负担，尝试屏蔽这些爬虫，导致部分用户被误拦。若用户使用的是最新浏览器却被拦截，可联系作者提供浏览器信息以解决问题。此外，使用archive.*（如archive.today、archive.ph）的用户也被误认为恶意爬虫，建议改用更规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同操作系统和文件系统中关于inode 0的处理及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• **the_mitsuhiko**：根据OpenBSD和Linux的文档，inode 0不能用于常规用途。例如，Linux内核不会将inode 0分配给共享内存，因为用户空间（如glibc）依赖于inode编号非零。macOS中也明确指出，inode 0是保留的，用户应该跳过d_fileno为0的目录项。

• **jcalvinowens**：过去Linux的tmpfs中曾经允许inode 0，但现在内核已经不允许。jcalvinowens分享了一次在生产环境中遇到的实际问题，由于目录中有inode为0的文件导致服务无法重启，最终通过getdents()发现问题。

• **etbebl**：对撰写此类文章的目的提出质疑，认为揭示这些细节可能会诱导人们利用这些系统特性，从而导致更多错误和更难理解的系统行为。etbebl认为这可能是一种不必要的复杂化。

• **nulld3v**：提到内核中正在努力推动用户空间不再依赖inode编号，因为难以保证跨重启的唯一性和稳定性。引用了一个YouTube视频讨论这个问题。

• **Animats**：指出用户空间看到的"inode"与文件系统内部的表示早已不再直接相关，暗示用户空间对inode的依赖可能是不必要的。

• **duckerude**：引用了Rust语言的一个讨论，提到文件描述符不能是-1，但并未明确禁止其他负数。Rust的标准库因此只禁止-1，而仍允许例如-2。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应该揭示和利用这些底层细节。etbebl认为这样做可能会导致系统更加复杂和不可靠，而其他评论者则更多从技术细节和实际问题角度讨论。
• 实际遇到的inode 0问题以及如何通过底层工具（如getdents()）发现和解决问题也是一个重要讨论点。
• 推动用户空间不再依赖inode编号以提高系统稳定性和简化设计是未来发展的一个方向。

You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: Show HN: MBCompass – Android Compass App
data.author: nativeforks
data.article_summary: MBCompass是一款功能齐全的指南针应用，使用Jetpack Compose开发，通过设备的磁力计和加速度计提供实时地磁场更新，支持显示磁北、当前位置（使用OpenStreetMap）、明暗主题、屏幕常亮、横屏模式及流畅的指南针旋转。应用结合传感器融合技术（加速度计、磁力计和陀螺仪）提高准确性，无广告和应用内购买。用户可以自由使用、研究、分享和改进该应用，遵循GPL-3.0开源许可证。贡献和反馈欢迎。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕开源、隐私友好的指南针应用及其相关问题的讨论

不同观点：
• @nativeforks 认为开发动力源自热情以及创造有用和干净事物的喜悦，重点在于被重视FOSS（自由和开放源码软件）、隐私和道德软件的人发现，而不是为了出名。他还提到像Aurora或F-Droid这样的替代应用商店更容易让这类应用被发现。

• @AshamedCaptain 提到了一个具体的指南针应用（https://github.com/Kr0oked/Compass），并认为其性能接近iPhone的指南针应用，但相比之下，TFA（可能指另一个指南针应用）显得迟缓，推测是由于平滑处理的效果。

• @anonymousiam 指出互联网对于更新位置的磁偏角常数是有用的，否则指南针在所有位置的准确性不高，并提供了一个学习资源（https://www.rei.com/learn/expert-advice/compass-declination）。

• @weinzierl 分享了自己的经历，提到在封闭的生态系统中发布免费和道德的应用是一个艰难的过程，指出苹果和谷歌不喜欢从免费应用中获取30%的抽成，因此这类应用很少见。他认为这是更深层次的原因。

补充讨论：
• @ianburrell 建议应用能显示真北而不仅仅是磁北，并提到位置应该提供磁偏角。

• @h-c-c 质疑应用为什么需要网络权限，暗示对隐私的关注。

• @esafak 询问是否可以把应用做成小部件，以便一直显示在屏幕上。

• @leecommamichael 则简单地问Android是否自带指南针应用。

争议焦点：
• 应用在封闭生态系统（如苹果和谷歌的应用商店）中的发布难度以及这些公司对免费应用的态度是讨论的一个争议点。@weinzierl 的经历表明，免费和道德的应用在主流平台上发布面临很大挑战，主要因为这些平台的商业模式。

• 应用的隐私问题也被提出，@h-c-c 对网络权限的必要性表示怀疑，反映了用户对隐私的关注。

这些观点共同构成了对开源、隐私友好的指南针应用开发和使用的多角度讨论，涉及技术性能、隐私问题、应用发布挑战等多个方面。

• 应用在封闭生态系统（如苹果和谷歌的应用商店）中的发布难度以及这些公司对免费应用的态度是讨论的一个争议点。@weinzierl 的经历表明，免费和道德的应用在主流平台上发布面临很大挑战，主要因为这些平台的商业模式。

• 应用的隐私问题也被提出，@h-c-c 对网络权限的必要性表示怀疑，反映了用户对隐私的关注。

这些观点共同构成了对开源、隐私友好的指南针应用开发和使用的多角度讨论，涉及技术性能、隐私问题、应用发布挑战等多个方面。

What is Agno?
Agno
is a full-stack framework for building Multi-Agent Systems with memory, knowledge and reasoning.
Use Agno to build the 5 levels of Agentic Systems:
Level 1: Agents with tools and instructions.
Level 2: Agents with knowledge and storage.
Level 3: Agents with memory and reasoning.
Level 4: Agent Teams that can reason and collaborate.
Level 5: Agentic Workflows with state and determinism.

Get Started
If you're new to Agno, read the documentation to build your
first Agent
, chat with it on the
playground
and monitor it on
agno.com
.
After that, checkout the
Examples Gallery
and build real-world applications with Agno.
Why Agno?
Agno will help you build best-in-class, highly-performant agentic systems, saving you hours of research and boilerplate. Here are some key features that set Agno apart:
Model Agnostic
: Agno provides a unified interface to 23+ model providers, no lock-in.
Highly performant
: Agents instantiate in
~3μs
and use
~6.5Kib
memory on average.
Reasoning is a first class citizen
: Reasoning improves reliability and is a must-have for complex autonomous agents. Agno supports 3 approaches to reasoning: Reasoning Models,
ReasoningTools
or our custom
chain-of-thought
approach.
Natively Multi-Modal
: Agno Agents are natively multi-modal, they accept text, image, audio and video as input and generate text, image, audio and video as output.
Advanced Multi-Agent Architecture
: Agno provides an industry leading multi-agent architecture (
Agent Teams
) with reasoning, memory, and shared context.
Built-in Agentic Search
: Agents can search for information at runtime using 20+ vector databases. Agno provides state-of-the-art Agentic RAG,
fully async and highly performant.
Built-in Memory & Session Storage
: Agents come with built-in
Storage
&
Memory
drivers that give your Agents long-term memory and session storage.
Structured Outputs
: Agno Agents can return fully-typed responses using model provided structured outputs or
json_mode
.
Pre-built FastAPI Routes
: After building your Agents, serve them using pre-built FastAPI routes. 0 to production in minutes.
Monitoring
: Monitor agent sessions and performance in real-time on
agno.com
.

pip install -U agno

data.title: OneDrive File Picker Flaw Provides Apps Full Read Access Entire OneDrive
data.author: ano-ther
data.article_summary: 微软的OneDrive文件选择器存在一个安全漏洞，导致网站可以访问用户的整个OneDrive内容，而不仅仅是用户选择上传的文件。该漏洞影响数百个应用程序，包括ChatGPT、Slack、Trello和ClickUp，可能导致数百万用户的OneDrive数据面临泄露风险。漏洞的原因包括OneDrive文件选择器请求过度的读取权限以及OAuth范围不精细，加上微软提示信息不明确，使用户容易意外授予全盘访问权限。敏感的访问令牌还可能被明文存储在浏览器中，增加风险。为减轻风险，用户应检查并撤销不必要的第三方应用访问权限，开发者应避免使用刷新令牌，并考虑使用更安全的文件共享方式。微软正考虑改进这一问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软OneDrive的OAuth权限管理及其安全性

不同观点：
• 一种观点质疑微软的设计是否是故意而为之，并暗示这可能是微软Windows系统常见问题的一个体现。该评论带有讽刺意味，认为微软未来的改进也未必能解决问题（[type0]）。

• [pawanjswal] 提出OneDrive文件选择器的OAuth权限管理存在问题，认为在2025年仍然没有实现细粒度的权限控制是不合理的。他指出，为了上传一个文件而授予整个驱动器的读取权限，违背了最小权限原则。这暗示微软在权限管理上存在安全性和隐私性的不足。

• [mchenier] 提供了一种解决方案，通过创建一个虚拟的OneDrive账户并共享特定文件夹，从而限制第三方应用访问主账户的全部文件。这种方法旨在减少攻击面并保护主账户的隐私和安全。这种观点更倾向于从用户角度出发，提供实际操作建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于OneDrive的权限管理是否合理，尤其是OAuth权限的范围。一方认为这是设计缺陷，另一方提供了解决方案以减轻潜在风险。

• 讨论还涉及用户隐私和安全问题，特别是在第三方应用访问用户数据时的权限控制。这反映了用户对数据隐私和应用安全的关注。

• [mchenier] 的解决方案提供了一种实际操作的可能性，显示了在现有系统限制下，用户如何自行采取措施保护自己的数据隐私。

OneDrive File Picker Flaw Provides ChatGPT and Other Web Apps Full Read Access to Usersâ Entire OneDrive
The Oasis Research Team
Cyber Research Team
Published on
May 28, 2025
Read Time
8

Share
Table of Contents
Heading 2
Heading 3
Oasis Security's research team uncovered a flaw in Microsoft's OneDrive File Picker that allows websites to access a userâs entire OneDrive content, rather than just the specific files selected for upload via OneDrive File Picker. Researchers estimate that hundreds of apps are affected, including ChatGPT, Slack, Trello, and ClickUpâmeaning millions of users may have already granted these apps access to their OneDrive. This flaw could have severe consequences, including customer data leakage and violation of compliance regulations.
Upon discovery, Oasis reported the flaw to Microsoft and advised vendors using OneDrive File Picker of the issue. In response, Microsoft is considering future improvements, including more precise alignment between what OneDrive File Picker does and the access it requires.Â
Below are details of the flaw and mitigation strategies. You can read the Oasis Security Research teamâs full report
here
.
â
The FlawsÂ
Excessive Permissions in the OneDrive File Picker
The official OneDrive File Picker implementation requests read access to the entire drive â even when uploading just a single file â due to the lack of fine-grained OAuth scopes for OneDrive.Â
While users are prompted to provide consent before completing an upload, the promptâs vague and unclear language does not communicate the level of access being granted, leaving users open to unexpected security risks.
The lack of fine-grained scopes makes it impossible for users to distinguish between malicious apps that target all files and legitimate apps that ask for excessive permissions simply because there is no other secure option.
â
Insecure Storage of Sensitive Secrets
Sensitive secrets used for this access are often stored insecurely by default.
The latest version of OneDrive File Picker (8.0) requires developers to take care of the authentication themselves, typically using the Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) and most likely using the
Authorization Flow
.Â
Security risks ensue:
MSAL stores sensitive Tokens in the browserâs session storage in plain text.Â
With Authorization Flows a
Refresh Token
may also be issued, which lengthens the access period, providing ongoing access to the user's data.Â
Notably, OpenAI uses version 8.0.
â
Mitigation Steps
The lack of fine-grained OAuth scopes combined with Microsoftâs vague user prompt is a dangerous combination that puts both personal and enterprise users at risk. Oasis Security recommends that individuals and technology leaders review the third-party access theyâve granted to their account to mitigate the potential risks raised by these issues.
â
Check Whether or Not Youâve Previously Granted Access to a Vendor
â
How to for Private Accounts
Log in to your Microsoft Account.
In the left or top pane, click on "Privacy".
Under "App Access", select the list of apps that have access to your account.
Review the list of apps, and for each app, click on âDetailsâ to view the specific scopes and permissions granted.
You can âStop Sharingâ at any time. Consider that an Access Token takes about an hour to expire regardless of when you clicked stopped sharing.
This would however revoke a Refresh Token if present.
â
How to for Organizations
In the Entra Admin Center, navigate to the
list of enterprise applications
.
The list will display an Application ID column (Client ID) and an Object ID column (also known as the Service Principal Object ID).
Currently, there is no way to filter for Delegated Applications directly from this screen.
To check the permissions granted to each app, click on an application, then click on the âPermissionsâ button in the left pane. This will list all granted scopes and you can verify whether they are delegated.
You can also view the user who granted the permissions.
â
Check if a Site Uses the OneDrive File Picker
To check if a site is using the OneDrive File Picker:
Attempt to upload or download a file to OneDrive through the site's interface.
When the consent prompt appears, check whether OneDrive permissions are being requested.
â
Mitigation for Web Apps
If possible, temporarily remove the option to upload files using OneDrive through OAuth until Microsoft provides a secure alternative. In the meantime, consider exploring safer, simpler workarounds, such as supporting shared "view-only" file links from OneDrive, understanding that this flow may be less convenient for users.
If removing the File Picker is not a feasible solution for you, Oasis Security recommends the following:
Avoid using Refresh Tokens
Do not request the "offline ac

data.title: Revisiting Loop Recognition in C++ in Rust
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文比较了2011年和2024年不同编程语言的流行度和特性变化。2011年，Google在一份报告中比较了C++、Java、Go和Scala的算法实现。当时，Java最受欢迎，Scala则非常小众。到2024年，Stack Overflow调查显示，Java和C++的流行度下降，Go和Rust则显著上升，特别是Rust成为备受推崇的语言。Rust以其性能、类型安全和并发性著称，通过借阅检查器在编译时确保内存安全，而非使用垃圾回收机制。文章还提到一个循环识别算法，用于不同语言的基准测试，尽管具体算法描述较为简略。总体而言，Rust作为新竞争者，正改变编程语言的格局。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Raspberry Pi OS中的开发工具版本和代码实现问题

不同观点：
• [kvemkon] 提到在Raspberry Pi OS（Bookworm版本）中，g++编译器的版本较为过时（12.2.0），而cargo（Rust的包管理工具）版本较新。他指出用户要么继续使用过时的g++和Rust版本，要么从Debian的实验性仓库中安装较新的g++版本（如gcc-15）。

• [pjmlp] 对C++代码的实现提出质疑，认为代码没有采用C++23的最佳实践，尤其指出在现代CPU缓存行环境下，使用`std::list`可能不是最佳选择。他暗示代码没有充分利用现代C++特性和硬件优化。

• [krona] 对C++的并查集（union/find）算法中的`FindSet()`实现提出批评，特别指出该实现构建了一个临时列表，认为这种做法不合适，甚至用"Incredible scenes"（令人难以置信的场景）来形容。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是开发工具版本的滞后与代码实现的现代化需求之间的矛盾。
• 另一个焦点是对具体算法实现（如并查集）的合理性质疑，特别是针对`std::list`的使用和临时列表的创建。
• 讨论还涉及硬件优化问题，[pjmlp]指出代码可能没有很好地适应现代CPU的缓存行特性。

整体来看，讨论围绕工具链的版本更新和代码实现的现代化、优化展开，涉及开发环境的配置和算法实现的合理性。

44131307.article_content:
Back in 2011, Google published
a report
for Scala Days 2011 comparing the idiomatic implementation of an algorithm in C++, Java, Go, and Scala.
1
Over ten years later, the landscape has changed
significantly
.
1
C++ and Java were logical choices at the time. Go was the fresh hotness at Google. Scala... Scala Days
The
2011 Stack Overflow Survey
2
(the second ever!) only asked users what languages they were proficient in. Let's pretend for a moment that proficency roughly correlates to popularity. Java leads the four with nearly 32% of respondents claiming some proficiency. C++ is in eighth with just over 26%. Scala gets a measly 0.5%, which puts it all the way into
nineteenth
place. And Go, having been introduced to the public only two years before, only has a single vote. Rust appears to have zero responses, which makes sense considering that it was a pet project until 2009 and wasn't stable until 2015.
2
The 2011 SO Survey used SurveyMonkey and linked to the results. That link no longer works. I had to download the raw data and crunch the numbers myself. Since I didn't look at all the single-vote responses, it's likely that I missed a few points. It's unlikely that those points will cause any change in place for this comparison.
3
3
If you're curious about the top 5: SQL 57.4%, JavaScript 50.5%, CSS 48.2%, C# 48.1%, Java 31.9%
The
2024 Stack Overflow Survey
asks some more interesting questions. Proficiency is replaced with popularity (languages users have worked with in the past year), and we also get to see which languages are "admired" (languages that users wish to continue using), and "desired" (languages users have not used, but want to). Starting with popularity, Java falls to seventh place with 30.3% of respondents having used it in the past year, C++ is in ninth with 23%, Go reaches a whopping 13.5% for thirteenth place, Rust is actually on the map now at 12.6% and fourteenth place, and Scala gets 2.6% and twenty-sixth place. The results for admired languages paint a slightly different picture. Rust is the most admired language with more than 80% of respondents wanting to use it again. Go sees just over 67%, Scala just over 50%, C++ around 53%, and Java around 48%. It's fair to say that Rust is a new contender to this race.
The New Contender
As does the paper, we will introduce Rust by regurgitating Wikipedia.
Rust
is a general-purpose programming language emphasizing performance, type safety, and concurrency. It enforces memory safety, meaning that all references point to valid memory. It does so without a traditional garbage collector; instead, memory safety errors and data races are prevented by the "borrow checker", which tracks the object lifetime of references at compile time.
And a quick rundown of core properties matching the beats of the original paper:
Like C++ and Go, Rust is statically compiled
Rust is not garbage collected, opting for compile-time verification of memory lifetime through the borrow checker.
Rust has pointers but deferefencing these pointers is limited to
unsafe
contexts.
Rust requires statements be terminated with
;
. Lines not terminated with
;
are considered expressions, returning their value.
4
Rust does not
enforce
a specific coding style but highly encourages it by including
rustfmt
as part of its toolchain.
Rust has very powerful type inference, making type declarations rare.
5
Rust is
not
object-oriented, though it does feature methods as a syntactic sugar.
4
It seems odd to put a focus on line terminators as a core property of a language. Putting on the Conspiracy Hat, it feels like there was a plan to shill Go until the benchmark results came out.
5
Since this paper was released, C++ also gained type inference through the
auto
keyword. In some cases, this inference is more powerful than Rust. In others...
With all that out of the way, let's Rewrite It In Rust.
The Algorithm (The It)
The original paper uses an implementation of a loop recognition algorithm as a benchmark. The description of the algorithm in the original paper was brief, only referencing the relevant papers
6
7
and providing an exact copy of the pseudocode.
6
Havlak, Paul. (1997). Nesting of Reducible and Irreducible Loops. ACM Trans. Program. Lang. Syst.. 19. 557-567.
10.1145/262004.262005
.
7
Tarjan, Robert. (1973). Testing Flow Graph Reducibility. Journal of Computer and System Sciences. 9. 96-107.
10.1145/800125.804040
.
What the algorithm actually does is irrelevant to this experiment. The reasons for choosing this algorithm over others is describe in the original paper. But since I was asked to actually describe loop recognition, I will make an attempt.
8
8
You are better off reading the Havlak paper.
