data.title: A man who sailed round the world with a chicken (2019)
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了法国水手Guirec Soudée与他的鸡伴侣Monique环游世界的冒险经历。在长达五年的时间里，他们航行了45,000英里，穿越大西洋，前往南北极，并经历了各种冒险和灾难。Guirec在独自航行中曾被北极冰困住130天，遭遇15米高的巨浪，还曾被加拿大海岸警卫队短暂拘押。他的旅程充满了惊险和趣味，而他的鸡Monique则一直陪伴左右，甚至成为了互联网上的明星。他们的故事被记录在社交媒体上，吸引了大量粉丝，并已出版了一本儿童书《环游世界的母鸡》。Guirec在布列塔尼的一个小岛上长大，自小热爱海洋，渴望冒险，最终实现了这一壮举。

44129480.article_content:
‘Why did the chicken cross the globe?’: Monique accompanied Guirec Soudée on his travels around the world.
Photograph: Phil Fisk/The Observer
View image in fullscreen
‘Why did the chicken cross the globe?’: Monique accompanied Guirec Soudée on his travels around the world.
Photograph: Phil Fisk/The Observer
Adventure travel
This article is more than
6 years old
Have hen will travel: the man who sailed round the world with a chicken
This article is more than 6 years old
Meet Monique, for the past five years, she and Guirec Soudée have been sailing around the world. Emma Beddington reveals how the French sailor chose to brave the high seas with just one feathered shipmate
Emma Beddington
Sun 21 Apr 2019 01.00 EDT
Last modified on Thu 25 Apr 2019 05.27 EDT
Share
A
t the tip of Brittany’s wild, wet Côtes-d’Armor peninsula is the village of Plougrescant. Beyond that, butting right out into the sea, lies Yvinec island, a tiny outcrop intermittently accessible depending on tides via a rock-studded expanse of dunes and seaweed. To get there I have taken two planes, a train and a puzzling automobile. It has been an epic journey, but I can’t possibly say that to
Guirec Soudée
when he picks me up for the last leg in his 4x4. I may have got lost in a Brest industrial estate at midnight, unable to make the hire car headlights work, but the 26-year-old Breton sailed around the world solo for five years. During that time he was trapped in Arctic ice for 130 days, survived 15m waves, nearly capsized repeatedly, was imprisoned briefly by Canadian coastguards and became the youngest sailor to navigate the formidable Northwest Passage between the Pacific and the Atlantic solo. Well, I say solo. Sole human. He was accompanied by a chicken, a Rhode Island Red named Monique.
I said to myself, ‘If she annoys me, I can always eat her.’ It feels weird to say that now! We formed a real bond
From January 2014 to their return to Brittany in December 2018, the pair covered 45,000 miles. They crossed the Atlantic, travelled to the North and South Poles, across to Cape Horn, back to the Caribbean and home, punctuated by stops to repair the boat, wait out the weather, or earn money. Every adventure, encounter and disaster (there were plenty of all three) was recorded in jaw-dropping pictures and funny videos on their increasingly popular social media accounts (they now have 125k
Facebook
and 42.8k
Instagram
followers).
That was where I discovered – and fell hard for – the pair. A handsome, fresh-faced young adventurer and his stoic brown hen on their plucky little boat felt like a gift: an uncomplicated shot of sunshine in a dark time. Their story is an internet-age
Boy’s Own
adventure: Guirec paddleboarded through icebergs, met polar bears, caught huge fish and even saved a drowning poodle.
View image in fullscreen
Best dressed chicken: Monique braves the Greenland cold in her jumper.
Photograph: Guirec Soudée
Meanwhile Monique shared his breakfast (and, indeed, his paddleboard), bewitched Inuit kids who had never seen a hen, and perched on deck, contemplating the vastness of various oceans. No surprise then, to learn that their children’s book,
The Hen Who Sailed Around
the World
, has already been published.
Guirec (
sans
Monique) meets me in Plougrescant’s car park – a slight, garrulous and smiley figure in a big jumper – and we head off at a slow trundle across the bay to Yvinec. It is a private island (acquired cheaply after the war by the Soudée family), current population four. In addition to Guirec and Monique, there’s Bosco the dog, a rangy part-husky giant who waits on the headland to greet us. (“I got him in Alaska: I swapped him for a chainsaw.”) Girlfriend Lauren, who met Guirec through his Facebook page, is the fourth, part-time resident, helping out with his increasingly time-consuming social media commitments and public engagements. Guirec: “You’re sort of Breton now though, aren’t you?” Lauren (firmly): “No, I’m Parisienne.”
They share the handsome stone farmhouse in which Guirec grew up, a dreamy place with cornflower-blue doors and shutters and huge open fires. The sea is everywhere: we take a tour, clambering up the rocks so Guirec can point out the inlets, coves and best crabbing spots of his stretch of windswept coast. If ever a place were perfectly designed to raise an ocean-going adventurer, it’s here. His was a wild childhood: the youngest of eight siblings raised by an indulgent father, he was largely left to amuse himself. “I spent more time on water than on land. I got my first boat at seven and even before that, I would go out to sea to drop off my lobster pots and catch fish. This island made me.”
View image in fullscreen
Hen party: Guirec Soudée and Monique in the galley.
Photograph: Guirec Soudée
Sea always won over school: Guirec went to 13 in total, leaving with no qualifications, but a nagging desire for adventure. “When I turned 18, I could have got a job, but I wanted to travel. I wanted to go far awa

data.title: ReasoningGym: Reasoning Environments for RL with Verifiable Rewards
data.author: t55
data.article_summary: 《REASONING GYM: Reasoning Environments for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards》一文介绍了一个名为Reasoning Gym (RG)的库，用于强化学习中的推理环境，并提供可验证的奖励。该库包含超过100个数据生成器和验证器，涵盖代数、算术、计算、认知、几何、图论、逻辑以及多种常见游戏等多个领域。其主要创新在于能够生成几乎无限的训练数据，且复杂性可调，不同于以往固定的推理数据集。实验结果显示，RG在评估和强化学习推理模型方面具有良好效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Reinforcement Learning (RL) 在复杂推理任务中的应用及其有效性

不同观点：
• [phh] 认为将RL任务称为“推理”或“思考”有些言过其实。他指出，这些任务可以在没有真正“思考”的情况下完成，并表达了对创建一个包含多种RL任务的“RL Zoo”的期待，希望该项目能够长期维护并接受外部贡献。
• [jimmySixDOF] 分享了关于RL中“虚假奖励”现象的研究，展示了即使使用完全随机或错误的奖励，模型在数学基准测试中仍能取得显著进展。他还提到了使用内在反馈进行学习的RLIF框架及其在无需外部奖励的情况下实现有效学习的潜力。
• [starzmustdie] 提供了与Reasoning Gym相关的GitHub链接，为讨论增加了实际的资源支持。
• [ninakostoska] 提到NVIDIA的最新推理模型已经大量使用Reasoning Gym作为其数据混合的一部分，表明这一工具在实际应用中的重要性。
• [sadboots] 对在GSM8K（一个数学问题数据集）上过度拟合的问题表示担忧，呼吁在该数据集上进行更多样化的实验。

补充讨论：
• RL任务是否真正涉及“推理”和“思考”是讨论的一个焦点，phh对此持怀疑态度。

Abstract:
We introduce Reasoning Gym (RG), a library of reasoning environments for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. It provides over 100 data generators and verifiers spanning multiple domains including algebra, arithmetic, computation, cognition, geometry, graph theory, logic, and various common games. Its key innovation is the ability to generate virtually infinite training data with adjustable complexity, unlike most previous reasoning datasets, which are typically fixed. This procedural generation approach allows for continuous evaluation across varying difficulty levels. Our experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of RG in both evaluating and reinforcement learning of reasoning models.

data.author: wertyk

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled TradExpert: Revolutionizing Trading with Mixture of Expert LLMs, by Qianggang Ding and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the financial domain has opened new avenues for quantitative trading, particularly through the use of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the challenge of effectively synthesizing insights from diverse data sources and integrating both structured and unstructured data persists. This paper presents TradeExpert, a novel framework that employs a mix of experts (MoE) approach, using four specialized LLMs, each analyzing distinct sources of financial data, including news articles, market data, alpha factors, and fundamental data. The insights of these expert LLMs are further synthesized by a General Expert LLM to make a final prediction or decision. With specific prompts, TradeExpert can be switched between the prediction mode and the ranking mode for stock movement prediction and quantitative stock trading, respectively. In addition to existing benchmarks, we also release a large-scale financial dataset to comprehensively evaluate TradeExpert's effectiveness. Our experimental results demonstrate TradeExpert's superior performance across all trading scenarios.

data.title: EasyTier – P2P mesh VPN written in Rust using Tokio
data.author: wucke13
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了去中心化系统的特点。去中心化系统中，不存在客户端和服务器之间的区分，不依赖任何中心化的服务，所有节点都是平等且独立的。这意味着每个节点都可以独立运行，无需中心控制，从而提高了系统的弹性和抗故障能力。这种架构常用于区块链和 peer-to-peer 网络中，以实现更高的安全性和隐私保护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：P2P技术的当前应用及其相关技术比较

不同观点：
• esafak认为P2P技术过去因带宽成本而兴起，并探讨其是否能应用于大语言模型的计算成本问题，提到了两个项目（Serving和Training）作为示例。
• ChocolateGod询问P2P技术与Nebula在性能上的比较，并提供了一个Nebula项目的链接。
• jrm4将P2P技术与Tinc进行比较，指出Tinc的易用性，并提到在安全性方面通过其他加密措施（如SSH和HTTPS）来保障。
• snthpy询问P2P技术与Tailscale的比较，指出Rust和Go语言是其中一个区别，并提供Tailscale项目链接。
• wucke13认为P2P技术与ZeroTier方向相似，但P2P技术是开源的，并提到在西方讨论较少。
• csomar对评论中提到的中国技术场景表示疑问，特别提到一个与浙江ICP备案相关的链接，不清楚是否为商业注册。
• akie担心使用P2P技术可能会无意中让自己的IP地址用于发送非法流量，对此表示不安。
• volemo关注P2P技术如何应对DPI审查技术，特别是成功阻挡WireGuard的情况。
• juancn提供了一个Github链接，但没有进一步的讨论。
• ThinkBeat对P2P节点的使用表示兴趣，询问节点作为出口节点的问题，以及公共节点的作用。
• Loranubi询问P2P技术是否可以替代Hamachi。
• unquietwiki认为P2P技术可能更适合作为Netmaker的竞争对手而非ZeroTier，并对其在商业用例中的可扩展性表示不确定。
• thenthenthen对访问文档页面表示困难，询问是否需要先运行服务。
• BobbyTables2对P2P技术和“.cn”域名表示担忧，担心其与中国的关系。

补充讨论：
• 技术比较：讨论中涉及多种P2P技术的比较，包括Nebula、Tinc、Tailscale和ZeroTier，关注性能、易用性和安全性等方面。
• 安全性：akie对使用P2P技术的安全性表示担忧，担心可能涉及非法流量。
• 地域性问题：csomar和BobbyTables2提到了中国技术场景和“.cn”域名的问题，反映了一些用户对地域性因素的关注。
• 实用性：用户对P2P技术的实际应用场景（如替代Hamachi、商业用例的可扩展性）表示关注。

争议焦点：
• P2P技术的应用安全性：akie对P2P技术可能带来的安全隐患表示不安，特别是在流量传输方面。
• 地域性因素：部分用户对与中国相关的内容（如“.cn”域名和ICP备案）表示疑虑。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕P2P技术的当前应用、技术比较、安全性及其潜在问题展开。

data.title: Cuss: Map of profane words to a rating of sureness
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: "cuss" 是一个提供多种语言脏话词汇列表的软件包，根据词汇作为脏话使用的确定性进行评分（0到2），但不表示词汇的 vulgar 程度。该包适用于自然语言研究，不建议用于制作脏话过滤器。它支持 Node.js、Deno 和浏览器，包含英语、阿拉伯语（拉丁字母）、西班牙语、法语、意大利语、葡萄牙语及欧洲葡萄牙语的脏话列表。每个列表导出一个包含词汇及其确定性评分的对象。该项目是开源的，欢迎贡献新词汇或语言，使用 MIT 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：言论审查和敏感词过滤在不同语境下的困难与争议

不同观点：
• **言论审查的复杂性与不可能性**：donatj分享了在教育软件中管理敏感词列表的经验，指出不同地区对冒犯性词汇的定义差异很大，试图让所有人满意是不可能的。他们的解决方案是标记需要教师审查的词汇，而不具体说明原因，这样减少了争议。donatj认为言论审查是一个最好避免的问题。

• **敏感词过滤的用户体验问题**：blueflow提到在实时聊天中，某个随机单词被审查掉，用户需要通过查阅Urban Dictionary来理解为什么某些词会被审查，尤其是涉及到地名时，给用户带来了困扰。

• **学术界中的敏感词使用**：PaulHoule提到在学术论文摘要中看到英语中的脏话，表明在某些学术环境中，敏感词的使用并不会引发太大争议。

• **语言命名的争议**：carlos-menezes对“欧洲葡萄牙语”这一名称提出质疑，认为如果要区分，巴西葡萄牙语应称为“美洲葡萄牙语”。

• **法语词汇评级的困惑**：GuB-42指出法语词汇评级中的一些不准确之处，例如一些常用词被评为污秽，而它们的非污秽意义却很常见。

• **词汇评级的合理性与严重性**：CSMastermind提到数据集中没有严重性的概念，导致一些无害的词汇与严重的侮辱性词汇被同等对待。

• **词汇评级的任意性与全面性问题**：mdaniel和thih9讨论了词汇评级的确定过程，质疑其是否具有任意性，以及零评级的意义何在。

• **词汇列表的完整性与实用性**：SamBam对词汇列表中的零评级和词汇缺失提出疑问，认为零评级在编程实用性上没有太大意义。

• **数据格式的改进建议**：Blackarea建议数据格式应为语言无关的格式，如CSV，以提高实用性。

• **代码变量命名中的幽默与冒犯**：BrandoElFollito分享了代码中因变量名引发的幽默事件，表明在技术环境中，某些命名可能引发意外的争议。

• **词汇评级的准确性和严重性**，以及如何在技术上实现更合理的词汇审查机制。

data.article_summary: HIP（Heterogeneous-Compute Interface for Portability）是一个C++运行时API和内核语言，允许开发者使用单一源代码为AMD和NVIDIA GPU创建可移植应用程序。其主要特点包括：薄层设计，性能接近直接使用CUDA；支持C++特性如模板、lambda表达式、类和命名空间等；开发者可使用最佳开发环境和工具。HIP还提供HIPIFY工具，自动将CUDA代码转换为HIP。开发者可针对CUDA或AMD平台进行性能调优。HIP文档开放源码，详细信息可在ROCm文档中找到。需要注意的是，HIP并非CUDA的直接替代品，开发者需手动调整代码以实现最佳性能。

What is this repository for?
HIP is a C++ Runtime API and Kernel Language that allows developers to create portable applications for AMD and NVIDIA GPUs from single source code.
Key features include:
HIP is very thin and has little or no performance impact over coding directly in CUDA mode.
HIP allows coding in a single-source C++ programming language including features such as templates, C++11 lambdas, classes, namespaces, and more.
HIP allows developers to use the "best" development environment and tools on each target platform.
The
HIPIFY
tools automatically convert source from CUDA to HIP.
Developers can specialize for the platform (CUDA or AMD) to tune for performance or handle tricky cases.
New projects can be developed directly in the portable HIP C++ language and can run on either NVIDIA or AMD platforms.  Additionally, HIP provides porting tools which make it easy to port existing CUDA codes to the HIP layer, with no loss of performance as compared to the original CUDA application.  HIP is not intended to be a drop-in replacement for CUDA, and developers should expect to do some manual coding and performance tuning work to complete the port.
Note
The published documentation is available at
HIP documentation
in an organized, easy-to-read format, with search and a table of contents. The documentation source files reside in the
HIP/docs
folder of this GitHub repository. As with all ROCm projects, the documentation is open source. For more information on contributing to the documentation, see
Contribute to ROCm documentation
.

data.article_summary: 作者Harley Kimball在三天内开发了一款应用程序，但遭遇两次黑客攻击，并从中吸取了重要教训。该应用是一个安全研究人员资料的聚合目录，前端连接到Supabase实例。最初计划允许用户自注册，但由于安全风险取消了该功能，却忽略了一些关键问题。第一次攻击是由于PostgreSQL视图泄露了用户邮箱，且未正确应用行级安全（RLS）策略。第二次攻击是因为虽然前端取消了自注册功能，但Supabase Auth仍允许通过邮箱/密码注册。关键教训包括：快速开发易产生安全漏洞，使用Supabase和PostgreSQL需深刻理解其安全模型，PostgreSQL视图不自动遵循RLS，未使用的认证功能应禁用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编程工具及"vibe coding"（氛围编码）对初创公司和个人项目的影响，尤其是其带来的安全问题。

不同观点：
• **[paxys]** 认为，AI编码工具和"vibe coding"降低了技术门槛，使得许多技术水平不高的人为了快速赚钱而开发项目，忽视了安全最佳实践。这与过去技术人员注重安全的情况形成对比。

• **[Kuraj]** 部分同意"vibe coding"可能导致安全问题，但认为像Postgres数据库的安全问题即便在手写代码中也可能遇到，因此不完全归咎于"vibe coding"。

• **[rahimnathwani]** 指出，问题不在于"vibe coding"，而在于将数据库直接暴露在互联网上。配置RLS（行级安全）比手写后端更难，因此小型应用可能更容易出错。

• **[_fat_santa]** 强调，所有数据库连接都应通过API进行"隔离"。通过API和中间件控制访问权限，可以避免直接操作数据库，从而提高安全性。

• **[ungreased0675]** 认为"vibe coding"是问题的一部分，但根本原因在于架构过于复杂，可能导致代码像“意大利面条”一样混乱。

• **[rowanseymour]** 担心大量不良代码被输入LLM（大型语言模型）生成更多不良代码，过度依赖LLM会导致开发者对自己所交付的代码缺乏理解。

• **[jjani]** 认为即便在"vibe coding"之前，许多使用Supabase的移动应用也存在相同的安全漏洞。RLS技术对于初学者有吸引力，但需要高度的自律才能安全使用，不如直接使用API或无服务器函数简单。

• **[antifa]** 以讽刺的语气评论，将未上锁的门被入侵比作配置错误的数据库，暗示这是基本的安全常识问题。

• **[jart]** 强调，将新项目放在互联网上必然会面临黑客攻击，需要有足够的技术能力来应对，LLM无法帮助解决这些问题。

• **[CyanLite2]** 批评"vibe coding"使个人创业项目成为现代传销式骗局，推出劣质产品，指望卖出后让别人解决问题。

• **[nkotov]** 提出，随着项目获得付费客户，可能会出现更高层次的"vibe coding"机会。

• **[emrah]** 认为，黑客攻击与数据库配置错误有关，而不仅仅是"vibe coding"的问题。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于"vibe coding"是否直接导致安全问题，还是更深层次的技术能力和架构问题。
- 部分评论者认为配置错误和安全问题在手写代码中也可能发生，不应完全归咎于"vibe coding"。
- 强调了安全配置和使用API隔离数据库访问的重要性，特别是在小型应用和个人项目中。
- 对LLM生成代码的担忧，主要在于开发者可能因此缺乏对代码的理解和掌控能力。

I vibe coded and shipped an app in three days. It got hacked. Twice. Hereâs what I learned.  ð§µ
The app is a directory that aggregates security research profiles across various platforms like @Hacker0x01 , @Bugcrowd , @github , and more. The frontend connects to a Supabase instance, and I built it using Lovable and Cursor. All automation that feeds data into the database is handled separately.
disclosedonline.com/directory
Originally, I planned to allow users to self-register using Supabase Auth and submit the profiles they wanted aggregated. As I started implementing this, I realized it would introduce risk as I'd need to manage both authentication (who users are) and authorization (what they're allowed to do) properly. I decided to scrap self-registration... but I missed something important. (More on that later.)
Bug #1: Leaking Emails:
In my first test, users were authenticated via Supabase, which required real email addresses. While inspecting network requests, I discovered that responses from the profiles table were exposing user email addresses, which is obviously bad if users ever trusted me with private info.
To fix it, I created a PostgreSQL view that queried only the fields I needed from profiles, excluding email. I updated the frontend to query that view instead. Seemed more secureâ¦ but I accidentally made things worse. (More on that soon.)
Launch & First Compromise:
After switching to the view and removing frontend insertion, I launched the app. I had Row-Level Security (RLS) enabled and thought read-only access meant I was safe.
Within 24 hours, a researcher showed they could insert, update, and delete records, even though the frontend didnât expose those endpoints and RLS should have blocked it.
Why? The view I created didnât respect RLS.
By default, PostgreSQL views execute with the privileges of the view owner. In my case, this was an admin role. Unless you define the view as SECURITY INVOKER, or apply extra guards, RLS policies on underlying tables are bypassed. That was the critical misconfiguration. I fixed it by revoking unsafe access to the view and restructuring how data is queried. Shoutout to the researcher who responsibly disclosed it (@Goofygiraffe06).
Second Compromise:
A day later, another researcher (@Kr1shna4garwal) reached out: they were able to create new profiles in the database, though (thankfully) they couldnât modify or delete existing ones.
This wasnât due to the view. Instead, I had left Supabase Auth enabled, even though I had removed self-registration from the frontend. That meant attackers could still register via email/password and act as authenticated users, subject to whatever RLS rules existed. After disabling sign-ups in Supabaseâs Auth settings, the issue was resolved.
Key Takeaways:
Vibe coding ships fast, but security holes are the default.
Supabase + Postgres are powerful, but itâs easy to misconfigure them if you donât understand their security model, especially around views and RLS.
If you use PostgreSQL views, remember: they donât automatically respect RLS policies.
Disable Supabase Auth if you're not using it - even if your frontend doesnât expose it.
Threat modeling matters. My app only handled public data, so the impact was low. If youâre handling PII/PHI, this kind of exposure could be catastrophic.
If you enjoyed this post, check out my newsletter: weekly bug bounty writeups, tools, and more: .

data.title: Understanding Consistency in Databases: Beyond the Basics
data.author: jgeraert
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了在处理数据库一致性时，仅依赖ACID特性可能不足以应对复杂场景，尤其是在并发事务处理中。作者通过一个Spring Boot/Java代码示例，展示了在处理5000条销售记录时，如何因并发问题导致分页缺失行、重复更新等问题。

文章首先演示了默认分页实现的问题（`/pagination-zero`），然后通过修复分页问题（`/pagination-zero-fixed`）展示如何在没有隔离级别时避免这些问题。最终，通过应用“可重复读”（`REPEATABLE READ`）隔离级别和乐观锁（`optimistic locking`）实现一致性并提升性能（`/repeatable-read`）。

文章还介绍了不同的隔离级别，包括“读未提交”、“读已提交”、“可重复读”和“可串行化”，并指出高隔离级别会牺牲性能。为解决这一问题，作者建议使用乐观锁策略，通过版本控制防止并发冲突。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据库一致性模型，特别是对"最终一致性"和"数据库一致性"概念的理解深度以及相关学习资源的需求。

不同观点：
• [tanseydavid的观点] 对"数据库一致性"概念有信心最终能够理解，但对"最终一致性"（Eventual Consistency）感到困惑，暗示对该概念的复杂性或抽象性感到困扰。

• [ashvardanian的观点] 认为目前的学习资源根据深度可以分类：中等深度的资源如Medium文章，中等深入的如Substack和公司博客，而深度技术探讨则来自于个人博客。同时，表达了对类似Jepsen这样的高质量技术分析（包括代码示例和实际使用中的细节及注意事项）的需求，期望看到更多这种深入探讨一致性模型的内容。

补充讨论：
• 对学习资源的分级：ashvardanian对不同平台上的技术内容进行了分类，提出了对深度技术分析的渴望，尤其是那些结合实际代码和应用场景的讨论。

• 对Jepsen系列内容的推崇：ashvardanian特别提到了Jepsen测试系列的内容，认为这是深入理解一致性模型的高质量资源，强调了实际代码和实现细节在学习中的重要性。

争议焦点：虽然没有直接的争论，但tanseydavid的困惑点可能代表了一部分学习者在面对"最终一致性"这一复杂概念时的普遍困难，而ashvardanian则更关注于如何找到高质量的学习资源来解决这些困惑。

44157116.article_content:
Understanding Consistency in Databases: Beyond basic ACID
Lucas Borsatto
Follow
8 min read
·
9 hours ago
--
Listen
Share
What to do when dealing with N multiple transactions at the same time?
Most of the time we perform CRUD operations under the pragmatic standard transactional scope, thinking it will suffice under all circumstances. After all, what could go wrong when we always apply a standard ACID tool provided by our frameworks, right? But it feels “good enough” only until we face corner cases of the real world production traffic: missing rows after pagination, duplicated updates, or metrics that refuse to add up.
Going deeper in the reasons of why to use more than the traditional transactional, scope can be hard without some real world examples of when or how should we use something different from what we use to. In this article I revisit those issues through a tiny Spring Boot/Java code base. The example we will use run through the following steps:
Paginate
5 000
Sale
rows whose status starts as
NOT_INITIALIZED
.
Publish
each id to a Kafka topic.
Consume
each message, updating its status to
PROCESSING
.
Demonstrate how plain idempotency checks and pagination fail under load.
Apply
REPEATABLE READ
isolation level and
optimistic locking
to restore consistency with much better performance.
Experiment set up
The article code can be found on
github here
. We will use a controller with three endpoints running different implementations of the proposed example:
// ExperimentController
@PostMapping("/pagination-zero")
public ResponseEntity<Void> pagination() {
Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> paginationZeroService.process(false));
return ResponseEntity.accepted().build();
}
@PostMapping("/pagination-zero-fixed")
public ResponseEntity<Void> paginationFixed() {
Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> paginationZeroService.process(true));
return ResponseEntity.accepted().build();
}
@PostMapping("/repeatable-read")
public ResponseEntity<Void> repeatable() {
Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> repeatableReadService.process());
return ResponseEntity.accepted().build();
}
We will use
/pagination-zero
to demonstrate the problem when we run on a default pagination implementation. After that we show why fixing pagination at 0 is necessary when no isolation level is applied, running the experiment on /
pagination-zero-fixed
endpoint. And on conclusion we show our final solution for the corner cases presented, running the
/repeatable-read
endpoint.
What is an Isolation Level?
We can think of isolation level to be the degree of
visibility
that CRUD operations have when two or more transactions are running concurrently. Taking our sales example in consideration, it would be translated to how much a transaction running the status update from
NOT_INITIALIZED
to
PROCESSING
can affect and be affected by other concurrent transactions.
By default, SQL databases support four types of isolation levels:
READ UNCOMMITED
: No guarantees, rarely used. Transactions are not independent, and even in flight operations which were not yet commited are seen by other transactions, what is know as dirty reads.
READ COMMITED
: Applied by default. Guarantees that in flight CRUD operations are not seem by other running transactions. Only commited changes performed before operation starts are seen, preventing dirty reads. But the same query performed in two diffent places of the transaction can read two different values, what is known as non-repeatable read.
REPEATABLE READ
: All operations inside the transaction see a stable snapshot of the data related to that query, preventing dirty and non-repeatable reads. But fails when business rules depend on seing if another transaction updated its rows values to evaluate if it can proceed. This event is known as write-skew.
SERIALIZABLE
: Performs each CRUD operation in sequence, making database execute only one operation per time through locks or by abort-and-retry. Prevent all cited anomalies.
So why not apply
SERIALIZABLE
directly? Cause the stronger the isolation level is, more you compromise your application performance. Under high workload, it may be impractical to apply such level depending on the circunstances. And that’s where
locking
strategies step in.
Locking strategies
Before we dive into the experiment itself, let’s refresh the two classic locking approaches:
Pessimistic locking : Usually applied implementing
FOR UPDATE
for row-level or
LOCK TABLE
for table-level directly on a query. It guarantees that no other transaction will alter the rows affected by this query by waiting locks to be released. It usually presents better performance when application shows significant more write workload than reads, because retries consume more resource under such circunstances.
Optimistic locking : Applies locking through adding a new column on desired table, which indicates the row version number or timestamp of the last update. When a transaction is about to affect a row, it has to check if its version of the row match

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钠燃料电池技术及其在航空领域的可行性与潜在问题

不同观点：
• **[pjc50]** 对钠燃料电池持怀疑态度：

data.title: Bohemians at the Gate?
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容与版权法的冲突及相关道德和法律问题

不同观点：
• Philipwhiuk认为OpenAI试图用人工智能取代人类创作，而不是像艺术家Kawano那样仅仅从已故艺术家Mondrian的作品中获得灵感。他主张限制AI只能使用已故艺术家的作品，以保护在世艺术家的版权。
• Scarmig则通过历史案例（如美国早期的知识产权盗窃）说明知识产权法是实践性的，应以激励知识生产为目的。他主张应给予AI生成内容广泛的合理使用权，以避免在法律上过于限制。
• Pet_Ant将视觉艺术的现状比作Ikea对家具行业的影响，认为AI会使商业化艺术变得不再可行，但个人艺术表达仍会存在。
• Energywut强调了规模的重要性，认为小规模的艺术借鉴与大规模的AI生成内容不可等同视之，前者是艺术创作的一部分，而后者则是工业化规模的复制。
• Riskable从法律角度分析，认为AI应被视为复印机，责任应归于使用者而非开发者，因为无法建立一个包含所有版权作品的数据库来防止侵权。
• Parpfish质疑为何AI受艺术启发被视为侵权，而人类艺术家受前辈启发却被视为正常，认为这种区分是事后和主观的。
• Samanbb认为现有版权法不适用于AI生成内容，主张在法律框架建立之前，应从道德上将AI带来的财富分配给曾为该技术提供创作基础的艺术家。
• Hoseja认为艺术家因社会依赖高强度宣传而享有特权地位，如今失去垄断地位是不可避免的。
• Hilift关注法律修订过程中的不确定性，引用具体法案修正案的失败案例来说明全球性问题难以通过单一国家的法律解决。
• Dhosek关注艺术家名字的使用是否构成侵权，认为即使不侵犯版权，使用Mondrian名字也可能侵犯道德权利。
• Niemandhier通过实例说明迪士尼等大公司对公共领域角色的控制，认为这些衍生作品不应受到版权保护。
• Kelseyfrog从社会关系角度分析版权法，认为将艺术完全法律经济化会抹杀艺术的社会和人文价值。
• Kleinmatic对文章本身进行了嘲讽，认为其缺乏重点。
• Zzzeek以讽刺的口吻表示，使用他人的作品是民主化过程，原创者应对此表示感谢。

补充讨论：
• 不同评论者对AI生成内容的合法性和道德性有不同看法，争议焦点在于AI是否应被视为工具（如复印机）还是创作者，以及如何在法律上平衡保护原创与促进创新的关系。
• 有人关注历史和国际视角（如美国早期工业盗窃历史、全球法律协调问题），有人则专注于具体案例分析（如Mondrian名字使用问题）。
• 艺术与经济的冲突也是讨论的重要部分，部分评论者认为将艺术完全经济化会失去其人文价值。

data.title: Reducing Cargo target directory size with -Zno-embed-metadata
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust项目中`target`目录占用过多磁盘空间的问题，尤其是在启用了增量编译和调试信息（debuginfo）的情况下。通过实验，作者展示了不同编译选项对目录大小的影响，发现两者都会显著增加空间占用。此外，Rust编译过程中生成的元数据（metadata）也会导致空间浪费，因为在`.rlib`和`.rmeta`文件中都会保存一份元数据。作者提出了一种避免元数据重复存储的方法，即通过编译器标志让元数据仅保存在`.rmeta`文件中，从而减少`target`目录的总大小。这一改进有望优化Rust项目的磁盘空间使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cargo中元数据处理是否构成向后兼容性破坏

不同观点：
• KolmogorovComp认为：当前情况下，将.rlib文件中的元数据视为公共API的一部分是不可思议的。他指出，如果某些开发者依赖于这些元数据，而它本身并没有被文档化，那么这种依赖不应该自动被视为一个破坏性变更。
  - 论据1：元数据存在于.rlib文件中，但这些文件是中间文件，不应视为公共API的一部分。
  - 论据2：如果某些功能未被文档化，开发者依赖这些未文档化的功能，不应该成为认定为破坏性变更的理由。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于.rlib文件中的元数据是否应被视为公共API。KolmogorovComp主张这些文件和其中的元数据是内部实现细节，而非公共API的一部分。因此，不构成破坏性变更。
- 另一个值得注意的点是开发者对未文档化特性的依赖是否应当受到保护。这涉及到软件开发中关于“隐式依赖”的广泛讨论，即在没有明确文档说明的情况下，项目团队是否应对这些依赖负责。

44158720.article_content:
Disk usage of the
target
directory is a commonly cited annoyance with Rust (and Cargo)
– in the last year’s
Annual Survey
,
it was the third most pressing issue of Rust users, right after slow compilation
1
and subpar
debugging experience. Given the “build everything from source” compilation model of Rust, and both debuginfo and incremental compilation being enabled by default in the
dev
Cargo profile, it is unlikely that the
target
directory will ever become
lean
and small. However, there are still ways of how we could reduce the
target
directory size by a non-trivial amount. I will describe a brand-new method of achieving that in this blog post.
Note that there are also initiatives to reduce the size of the
target
directory along the temporal axis, i.e. prevent it from ballooning over time (see
Cargo Garbage Collection
). This post is more about how to reduce the size of the target directory overall.
What takes up the space, anyway?
It is not the focus of this post to dive deep into exploring what exactly takes space in the
target
directory, but I still think that it is useful to provide at least some background on this. I took
my favourite work project,
hyperqueue
, and compiled
it in several modes to compare the resulting
target
directory sizes
2
, using
rustc 1.89.0-nightly (2eef47813 2025-05-22)
:
Optimizations
Incremental
Debuginfo
target
size [MiB]
No (
dev
)
No
No
462
No (
dev
)
Yes
No
677
No (
dev
)
No
Yes
870
No (
dev
)
Yes
Yes
1316
Yes (
release
)
No
No
396
From the results, it’s clear that both debuginfo and incremental compilation caches take a lot of
space on disk. It might be that we could do something to reduce either of these, but there is one
additional thing that (kind of unnecessarily) causes
target
directory bloat, which is not
easily observable in this table, and that is the metadata of the compiled Rust crates.
Cargo pipelining & metadata duplication
First, we need to briefly talk about how Rust compilation works (in very, very simplified terms).
When a Rust library crate (
rlib
) is compiled in a “standard” way (i.e. no
LTO
or other funny
business) with Cargo, the compiler generates (amongst other things) two main outputs:
Metadata, which contains information necessary to link to that crate from other Rust code.
Object code, which is the compiled assembly code of the Rust crate.
The interesting thing about this is that the final object code isn’t actually needed in order to start
compiling Rust code that depends on a said library, metadata is enough (the object code will only be
needed at the final linking step). Cargo makes use of this fact, and when it compiles your crate graph,
it uses a technique called
pipelining
.
Imagine that you have a binary that depends on crate
B
, which itself depends on crate
A
. When
compiling
A
, Cargo will tell the compiler (using
--emit=metadata,...
) to emit a
.rmeta
file
containing the metadata of
A
as soon as possible. Once that file is ready, we can start compiling
B
by passing it the
.rmeta
file of
A
, even though the object code of
A
is not ready yet,
and thus partially overlap the compilation of both crates, which improves compile times. I will borrow
(and slightly extend) a cute ASCII diagram from
Alex Crichton’s internals post
about pipelining
to succintly show how it works:
--- .rmeta of A generated
v
[-libA----|--------]
[-libB----|--------]
[-binary-----------]
0s        5s       10s       15s                25s
Pipelining has been enabled in Cargo for many years, so it’s nothing new, and if you use Cargo, you
are using pipelining every day, perhaps without even knowing about it. However, there is one
suboptimal thing in regard to disk space usage with the pipelining approach.
The problem is that once the process finishes, you will be left with two copies of the metadata of
each library on disk. The first copy is in the final
.rlib
file (along with the object code), and
the second copy is in the
.rmeta
file. As is usual with Cargo, this problem will balloon if you build
your project with multiple configuration options (different Cargo profiles, different compiler/linker
flags, etc.).
A related issue is that if you are compiling a library as a
dylib
,
so that you generate a Rust dynamic library (e.g.
.so
on Linux), that will also contain the
metadata, even though it should not be required to actually consume (call functions from) the
library at runtime. This can be annoying for people who ship Rust
dylib
s, even though that’s
usually not very common due to Rust currently not having a stable
ABI
.
Avoiding duplicated metadata
So, what can we do about it? Well, last year, I noticed that many years ago, the illustrious
@bjorn3
has
proposed
an idea to introduce a compiler flag
that would cause the metadata to
only
be included in the
.rmeta
files, and no longer be present
in the
.rlib/.so
library files. I liked this idea, and since there already was a
prototype
implementation
prepared, it didn’t seem that hard to push it over the finish line.

data.author: GeorgeHaldane

主要讨论点：随机数生成器（PRNG）库的设计与实现，包括API设计、跨平台一致性、安全性、性能以及与其他库的比较。

不同观点：
• OskarS认为API设计中提供默认的`rand()`函数是很好的做法，便于在不关心生成器细节时快速获取随机数。但他指出，如果API允许设置种子（seed），则会导致无法升级生成器算法而不破坏API契约，建议全局随机数生成器应始终基于熵（entropy）来种子化，并通过线程本地存储实现线程安全。他还以C++为例展示了如何实现这一设计。

• jll29赞赏了该库的全面性，但提到`std::random_device`在无法提供足够熵时回退到非随机性PRNG的问题，这在加密应用中是不可接受的。他建议根据使用场景区分处理，例如加密应用应直接报错，而非关键应用可以容忍一定的降级。

• spacechild1对跨平台一致性表示赞赏，但质疑`rand_choice()`函数可能返回了对局部变量的引用，这会导致未定义行为。

• zx2c4对使用ChaCha CSPRNG时的种子长度提出质疑，认为32或64位种子不足以保证安全性，并指出输出流在2^32块后循环的问题。

• zX41ZdbW解释了一种通过利用均匀分布整数的特性来快速生成近似正态分布数值的技巧，指出这种方法在非高精度需求的场景（如游戏开发、模糊测试）中非常有效。

• nzzn提到Xoshiro/Xoroshiro生成器的完整实现，并提供了相关文档和库链接，指出这些生成器在处理复杂随机数生成任务时具有优势。

• fluffyllemon询问该库与Abseil的随机库之间的比较。

• joiguru提到DEShawResearch的random123库，并询问是否进行了对比。

• Iwan-Zotow对性能测试结果表示怀疑，尤其是`std::minstd`和`std::mt19997`的性能数据。

• pantalaimon质疑是否还需要使用`getrandom()`，认为现代系统中该函数已经足够快。

• jeffbee赞赏了稳定统一整数分布的特性，并指出标准库对生成器输出有明确规定但对分布输出未明确规定的问题。

补充讨论：
- 涉及多个随机数生成器库的比较和参考，如Xoshiro、Abseil和random123。
- 安全性讨论集中在种子生成和熵源的选择，特别是在加密应用中的关键性。
- 性能优化和跨平台一致性是多个评论中提到的优点。

data.title: Cloudlflare builds OAuth with Claude and publishes all the prompts
data.author: gregorywegory
data.article_summary: 这篇文章概述了Cloudflare的workers-oauth-provider项目的更新历史。自2025年3月至5月，项目进行了多次代码提交和合并请求，主要包括修复类型导入、移除未使用代码、解决PKCE降级攻击问题、验证授权重定向、增加API处理程序、引入onError回调函数、以及提升测试覆盖率等。此外，项目从实验阶段进入Beta阶段，并进行了多次版本发布（0.0.2至0.0.5），还调整了GitHub Actions以使用PNPM并添加了Prettier配置以统一代码格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用LLM（如Claude）生成代码的可行性、效率及其实际应用中的问题

不同观点：
• **支持LLM辅助编码的观点**：
  - @gregorywegory 原本是AI怀疑论者，但在使用Claude生成并改进代码的过程中，发现其输出质量较高，经过人工审查和修正后，代码通过了安全审查。他认为这种方法可以提高生产力，特别是在经过严格审查的情况下。
  - @paxys 认为AI辅助编码是未来的发展方向，特别是在工程师审查和测试AI生成代码的情况下。他提到自己的一些编码尝试中遇到困难，但通过参考他人成功的经验，认为可能是自己提示词写得不够好。
  - @jes5199 基于自己的使用经验，表示使用Claude让他在绿地项目中更加高效，尽管认知负担增加，但工具的改进速度很快，进一步提升了他的生产力。
  - @ookblah 强调AI可以极大减轻开发中的认知负担，特别是在调试和初步代码生成方面，尽管仍需人工监督，但它已经能显著提高效率。

• **对LLM辅助编码持保留态度的观点**：
  - @infinitebattery 提到Claude在某些情况下生成的代码存在错误，且多次提示后仍无法修正，最终需要人工手动修复。他认为AI工具目前只能完成部分工作，在复杂情况下可能会遇到很大困难。
  - @multimoon 认为虽然AI可以加速任务，但仍需经验丰富的程序员监督和修正其输出，特别是在处理复杂任务时。他强调AI不能独立完成任务，且对新手开发者可能不利。
  - @_tqr3 分享了自己使用LLM构建Web应用时的负面经验，包括LLM在修复代码时陷入循环，或失去上下文的问题，认为目前仍需大量时间调整提示词，才能获得有用的结果。

• **对LLM应用场景的讨论**：
  - @wooque 认为AI在处理模板化、小型项目（如1200行代码的OAuth库）时表现出色，但对大规模或更复杂的项目，可能效率有限。
  - @EtienneK 对项目文档中“provider”的定义提出质疑，认为OAuth 2.1中没有明确定义这一术语，显示出AI在处理标准和协议时可能存在术语不一致的问题。

• **对LLM工具的实际操作问题讨论**：
  - @mehdibl 提到Claude在集成和配置应用方面仍有限制，特别是在添加应用后端支持方面，目前只处于封闭测试阶段，这限制了其在实际项目中的应用。
  - @thih9 对Claude的使用计划和配额提出疑问，关心是否在实际使用中会受到限制。

• **对LLM技术未来发展的讨论**：
  - @qsort 认为虽然LLM在辅助编码方面表现出一定潜力，但从提交历史看，仍需要大量人工干预，工具虽然能节省时间，但目前还未能彻底改变其对AI辅助编码的看法。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：LLM是否能在实际开发中独立生成高质量代码，尤其是在更复杂的场景中。虽然有支持者认为AI可以极大提高生产力，但批评者指出AI在处理复杂问题时仍需大量人工干预和修正。
- **效率问题**：讨论中多次提到使用AI生成代码是否比人工编写更快。部分人认为AI能显著加速编码过程，但也有开发者认为AI在某些情况下可能拖慢进度，特别是在调试和修正错误时。
- **对新手和未来开发者的影响**：一些评论者担心过度依赖AI工具可能对新手开发者不利，导致技能退化，而经验丰富的开发者则可能利用AI进一步提升自己的能力。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何入门并学习机器人技术，包括所需工具、课程、实践项目以及相关资源。

不同观点：

data.title: A Hidden Weakness
data.author: serge-ss-paille
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了一次耗时较长的漏洞排查过程，最终获得了宝贵的知识。主要讨论了Android平台上API版本控制的问题，某些符号（如ASystemFontIterator_open）仅在特定API级别后可用。为了避免链接错误，可以使用动态查找符号的方法，如`dlopen`和`dlsym`。文章进一步介绍了`__ANDROID_UNAVAILABLE_SYMBOLS_ARE_WEAK__`的用法，通过编译器属性`__attribute__((__availability__))`来处理符号的可用性问题。在未定义符号的情况下，符号会被标记为弱引用（WEAK），直接调用会导致段错误。为解决此安全隐患，Clang提供了`-Werror=unguarded-availability`标志，用于静态检查可能导致未定义弱引用的调用，从而在编译时捕获这些问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于弱符号（weak symbol）链接和编译器优化的技术讨论]

不同观点：
• 第一个观点（dcrazy）：评论者最初认为文章会讨论一种特定情况，即当使用链接器直接标记导入符号为弱符号时，优化器会移除与NULL的比较。这表明评论者认为弱符号链接和编译器优化之间存在特定的交互，特别是在处理NULL比较时可能会出现预期之外的行为。

• 第二个观点（隐含在评论后半部分）：评论者指出，如果开发者希望使用弱符号，必须使用编译器属性明确标记它们。这暗示评论者认为正确使用编译器属性是确保弱符号按预期工作的重要步骤，避免编译器优化引发问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然评论中没有直接的争论，但隐含的争议焦点可能是开发者在处理弱符号时是否应该依赖编译器的自动优化，还是应通过明确的编译器属性来控制这一行为。评论者显然倾向于后者，认为显式标记是必要的。

• 重要论据：评论者提到了弱符号和NULL比较的优化问题，这可能是一个技术上的陷阱，尤其是在不正确使用弱符号的情况下，会导致代码行为不符合预期。评论者通过指出“需要用编译器属性标记”来强调正确使用这些属性的重要性。

• 例子：评论中提到了“优化器移除比较到NULL”的具体例子，这为讨论提供了技术背景，表明在处理弱符号时，编译器的优化行为可能会导致实际代码行为与开发者的预期不符。

44159318.article_content:
A Hidden Weakness
May 29, 2025
Categories:
mozilla
This is the story of a bug hunt that lasted much longer than expected, but ended
with the dearest of all treasures:
knowledge
.
Let's draw some context: the Android platform defines different API levels.
Unsurprisingly, some symbols are only defined starting with a given API version.
For instance,
ASystemFontIterator_open
is only available starting at API 29.
Unconditionally trying to use
ASystemFontIterator_open
while targeting an
API older than 29 leads to a linker error (an undefined reference), which makes
sense because the symbol, well, does not exist at that API level.
So a native application that wants to use this symbol can either refuse to run on
older API, or use a combination of
dlopen
and
dlsym
to dynamically
lookup for the symbol and provide a fallback if it does not exist. The latter
approach is used on Fenix, the Android version of Firefox.
Introducing
__ANDROID_UNAVAILABLE_SYMBOLS_ARE_WEAK__
As an alternative to the features from
<dlfcn.h>
, Android build system makes
it possible to define
-D__ANDROID_UNAVAILABLE_SYMBOLS_ARE_WEAK__
, combine it
with a compiler check through
-Werror=unguarded-availability
and a runtime
check through
__builtin_available
. Here is an example:
// The header that defines ASystemFontIterator_open.
#include
<android/system_fonts.h>
...
// Runtime check for API level
if
(
__builtin_available
(
android
29
,
*
))
{
/* Reference to the actual symbol. Does not fail at link time because an
alternative weak definition is always provided by <android/system_fonts.h>*/
auto
*
iterator
=
ASystemFontIterator_open
();
...
}
There's a lot happening there, so let's dive in the wilderness of compiler
extensions.
<android/system_fonts.h>
ASystemFontIterator_open
is defined in
<android/system_fonts.h>
as:
ASystemFontIterator
*
_Nullable
ASystemFontIterator_open
()
__INTRODUCED_IN
(
29
);
The
_Nullable
attribute is an interesting topic, but it's a side quest we're
not going to explore today. The macro function
__INTRODUCED_IN(...)
is
defined in
<android/versioning.h>
as:
#define __INTRODUCED_IN(api_level) __BIONIC_AVAILABILITY(introduced=api_level)
And
__BIONIC_AVAILABILITY
is conditionally defined in the same header as:
#if defined(__ANDROID_UNAVAILABLE_SYMBOLS_ARE_WEAK__)
#define __BIONIC_AVAILABILITY(__what, ...) __attribute__((__availability__(android,__what __VA_OPT__(,) __VA_ARGS__)))
#else
#define __BIONIC_AVAILABILITY(__what, ...) __attribute__((__availability__(android,strict,__what __VA_OPT__(,) __VA_ARGS__)))
#endif
So in our case
ASystemFontIterator_open
is flagged either with
__attribute__((__availability__(android,introduced=29))
or
__attribute__((__availability__(android,strict,introduced=29))
.
Let's write a simple C code containing only the following:
$
cat
>
a.c
<< EOF
void foo(void) __attribute__((__availability__(android,introduced=29)));
void bar(void) __attribute__((__availability__(android,strict,introduced=29)));
void foobar(void) {
foo();
bar();
}
EOF
Compile and inspect it:
$
clang
--target
=
x86_64-linux-android21
-c
a.c
a.c:5:3:
error:
'bar'
is
unavailable:
introduced
in
Android
29
android
5
|

()
;
|
^

note:
'bar'
has
been
explicitly
marked
unavailable
here
2

void
bar
(
void
)
__attribute__
((
__availability__
(
android,strict,introduced
=
29
)))
;

^

error
generated.
ok, so the
strict
keyword implies a compilation error if we reference that
symbol while targeting a lower version. Good. Let's remove it:
$
cat
>
b.c
<< EOF
void foo(void) __attribute__((__availability__(android,introduced=29)));
void foobar(void) {
foo();
}
EOF
$
clang
--target
=
x86_64-linux-android21
-c
b.c
$
nm
b.o
w
foo
0000000000000000

$

-s

No compilation error, even though the symbol
foo
is marked as available only
for more recent API. Instead we end up with a symbol
foo
marked as
WEAK
(
w
) and
UND
(for undefined). Calling this symbol is equivalent to
dereferencing a
nullptr
and ends up with a segfault. Not super safe!
-Werror=unguarded-availability
Fortunately, Clang provides a dedicated warning
-Wungarded-availability
,
turned into an error through
-Werror=unguarded-availability

enables static checking for calls that would resolve into calling undefined weak
reference because of an
__availability__
mismatch.

data.title: ThorVG: Super Lightweight Vector Graphics Engine
data.author: elcritch
data.article_summary: ThorVG 是一个开源矢量图形库，专注于创建高效的矢量场景和动画。它支持多种基本图形（如线条、形状、填充、描边等）、文本（Unicode字符）和图片格式（如SVG、JPG、PNG等），并提供多种效果（如模糊、阴影、渐变填充等）。ThorVG 适用于多个平台，包括Linux、MacOS、Windows、移动平台和Web等，并支持多种渲染后端（如CPU/SIMD、OpenGL/ES、WebGPU）。它具备线程机制，可高效处理多任务，并支持SVG和Lottie动画。通过模块化设计，ThorVG 保证了轻量和易维护性，适合多种应用和系统集成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ThorVG与其他图形技术的比较及其在不同用例中的适用性

不同观点：
• chriswarbo认为Lottie在Web上的表现不如20年前的Macromedia/Adobe Flash，尤其是在复杂2D矢量动画的制作上。他提出了几种可能的替代方案，如SVG、JS+CSS过渡，并询问Lottie的能力和SMIL的现状。
• mindbrix指出ThorVG在WebGL中的抗锯齿质量不如软件渲染器，并且在Safari上无法播放，这限制了其跨浏览器兼容性。

• Fraterkes提到在Godot中使用ThorVG时遇到文本渲染的bug，表明该技术在某些具体应用中仍存在问题。
• elcritch分享了在Nim中使用ThorVG进行GUI后端实验的经验，显示出对ThorVG在不同编程语言中的潜在用途的兴趣。
• Riskofrain希望看到ThorVG在游戏引擎如Godot中的实现，并对比了其与Rive在矢量渲染方面的能力。
• MintPaw关心ThorVG是否具有抗锯齿蒙版功能，这是他从Skia转向其他工具的障碍。
• wiradikusuma询问ThorVG的比较对象及其在Flutter项目中的内存/磁盘占用情况。
• jitl和0x0203都将ThorVG与Skia和blend2D进行比较，关注代码大小、性能和多线程能力。
• __grob对ThorVG使用第三方工具DeepWiki作为文档页面表示不满，希望有正式文档。
• cantalopes质疑是否需要重新发明Macromedia Flash，暗示对重复开发类似技术的必要性持怀疑态度。

About ThorVG
Thor Vector Graphics is an open-source graphics library designed for creating vector-based scenes and animations. It combines immense power with remarkable lightweight efficiency, as
Thor
embodies a dual meaning—symbolizing both thunderous strength and lightning-fast agility. Embracing the philosophy of
simpler is better
, the ThorVG project provides intuitive, user-friendly interfaces while maintaining a compact footprint and minimal overhead.
​
The following list shows primitives that are supported by ThorVG:
Lines & Shapes:
rectangle, circles, and paths with coordinate control
Filling:
solid colors, linear & radial gradients, and path clipping
Stroking:
stroke width, join, cap, dash patterns, and trimming
Scene Management:
retainable scene graph & object transformations
Composition:
various blending and masking
Text:
unicode characters and horizontal text layout using the scalable fonts (TTF)
Images:
SVG, JPG, PNG, WebP, Raw Bitmap
Effects:
blur, drop shadow, tint, tritone and color replacement
Animation:
Lottie
Anti-aliased Shapes
Path-Clipping
Blending
Gaussian-Blur
Gradient Filling
SVG
Texturing
Drop-Shadow
Stroking
Masking
Text
Color Replacement
Supported Platforms
ThorVG is actively under development, continuously expanding its support for essential platforms as needed. The major platforms currently supported include:
Linux
MacOS
Windows
Tizen
iOS
Android
Web
Flutter
OpenVela
Godot
Expressif
NuttX
Structural Design
ThorVG is designed for a wide range of programs, offering adaptability for integration and use in various applications and systems. It achieves this through a single binary with selectively buildable, modular components in a building block style. This ensures both optimal size and easy maintanence.
If your program includes the main renderer, you can seamlessly utilize ThorVG APIs by transitioning drawing contexts between the main renderer and ThorVG. Throughout these API calls, ThorVG effectively serializes drawing commands among volatile paint nodes. Subsequently, it undertakes synchronous or asynchronous rendering via its backend raster engines. Additionally, ThorVG is adept at handling vector images, including formats like SVG, and it remains adaptable for accommodating additional popular formats as needed. In the rendering process, the library may generate intermediate frame buffers for scene compositing, though only when essential. The accompanying diagram provides a concise overview of how to effectively incorporate ThorVG within your system.
Render Backends
Today, ThorVG provides its own implementation of multiple raster engines, allowing you to choose the one that best suits your app and system preferences.
​
CPU/SIMD (Software)
OpenGL/ES
WebGL
WebGPU
​
ThorVG is ahead of the curve, particularly in the web ecosystem. WebGPU introduces next-generation APIs similar to Vulkan, leveraging compute shaders and providing low-overhead, modern GPU access for more aggressive optimization strategies and broader applications. Building on this, ThorVG fully supports vector rendering features within its specification on top of WebGPU. Additionally, by abstracting underlying hardware graphics accelerations such as Metal, Vulkan, and DirectX, ThorVG ensures seamless adoption across various systems, regardless of the installed hardware accelerations.
Threading
ThorVG incorporates a threading mechanism that aims to seamlessly acquire subsequent scenes without unnecessary delays. It operates using a finely-tuned task scheduler based on thread pools, encompassing various tasks such as encoding, decoding, updating, and rendering. This design ensures that all tasks can effectively leverage multi-processing capabilities.
​
The task scheduler has been meticulously crafted to conceal complexity, streamline integration, and enhance user convenience. Therefore, the policy it employs is optional, allowing users to select it based on their specific requirements.
SVG
ThorVG facilitates SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) rendering via its dedicated SVG interpreter. Adhering to the
SVG Tiny Specification
, the implementation maintains a lightweight profile, rendering it particularly advantageous for embedded systems. While ThorVG comprehensively adheres to
most of the SVG Tiny specs
, certain features remain unsupported within the current framework. These include:
Animation
Interactivity
Multimedia
SVG rendering capabilities as highlighted by ThorVG
Lottie
ThorVG supports the most powerful Lottie Animation
features
(
see dotLottie Player
). Lottie is an industry standard, JSON-based vector animation file format that enables seamless distribution of animations on any platform, akin to shipping static assets. These files are compact and compatible with various devices, scaling up or down without pixelation. With Lottie, you can easily create, edit, test, collaborate, and di
44157406.article_summary: ThorVG 是一个开源矢量图形库，专注于创建高效的矢量场景和动画。它支持多种基本图形（如线条、形状、填充、描边等）、文本（Unicode字符）和图片格式（如SVG、JPG、PNG等），并提供多种效果（如模糊、阴影、渐变填充等）。ThorVG 适用于多个平台，包括Linux、MacOS、Windows、移动平台和Web等，并支持多种渲染后端（如CPU/SIMD、OpenGL/ES、WebGPU）。它具备线程机制，可高效处理多任务，并支持SVG和Lottie动画。通过模块化设计，ThorVG 保证了轻量和易维护性，适合多种应用和系统集成。

data.title: The Atomic Airplane
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 《核动力飞机的故事》讲述了1980年代飞机核推进计划的老兵们录制了近13小时的演示和访谈，描述了制造核动力飞机的惊人努力。主要内容围绕热传导反应堆实验（HTREs），这些实验设备至今仍存放在爱达荷州EBR-I博物馆的停车场。MIT的Jake Hecla博士和John Webb等人将这些资料进行了数字化保存。文章还详细介绍了1946年至1961年期间，美国进行的一系列核动力飞机研究和实验，包括使用B-36测试机和HTREs反应堆实验。然而，由于导弹和核潜艇的发展，1961年该项目被取消。文章还展示了核动力喷气发动机和Convair NX-2飞机的模型设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：1950年代核动力飞机项目的相关技术和历史，及其现代意义与争议。

不同观点：
• **支持对核动力飞机项目的兴趣与分享**：[petalmind]和[acidburnNSA]分享了1957年苏联关于核动力飞机的书籍扫描以及美国类似的核推进飞机进展报告，表达了对这一历史技术探索的兴趣。[acidburnNSA]还提供了详细视频和博客链接，方便其他人深入了解。

• **质疑与批评**：[krunck]认为核动力飞机和类似的超音速低空导弹等项目不应该被建造，暗示这些项目可能存在危险性或不必要性。这一观点反映了对核技术军事应用的反对立场。

• **历史关联与辐射问题**：[loph]提到了与核动力飞机相关的美国乔治亚核飞机实验室，并指出该地区至今仍有辐射问题，暗示核技术实验可能带来的长期环境影响。

• **历史见证与个人经历**：[t1234s]提到UFO研究员Stanton Freedman声称参与过核动力飞机项目，暗示这类项目在历史上确实有过实际研究和开发。

• **对现代科技探索的反思**：[glimshe]提出是否还有像核动力飞机和早期图形用户界面一样的前沿科技项目正在开发，质疑现代科技是否失去了当年的"疯狂"创新精神。

• **轻松调侃与文化联想**：[waffletower]和[christkv]以轻松调侃的方式将核动力飞机与科幻作品《雷鸟神机队》和《辐射》游戏中的设计理念联系起来，表现出对该话题的娱乐化态度。

补充讨论：
• **实际遗存**：[webdoodle]提到在爱达荷国家实验室展示的核动力飞机引擎，提供了与现实中核动力飞机相关的实物证据，增加了讨论的历史和技术现实感。

争议焦点：核动力飞机项目的可行性、安全性及其历史与现代意义。一方面，有人对其历史和技术价值感兴趣，另一方面，有人认为这类项目不应被实际建造，因为存在辐射风险和潜在军事应用问题。

44130915.article_content:
The Story of the Atomic Airplane
In 1980s, veterans of the Aircraft Nuclear Propulsion program got together and
recorded nearly 13 hours of presentations and interviews describing the amazing
effort to make a nuclear-powered airplane.  The content is mostly focused on the
Heat Transfer Reactor Experiments (HTREs) which can still be seen sitting out in
the parking lot of the EBR-I museum in Idaho.
Dr. Jake Hecla, Stanton Postdoctoral Fellow at MIT, digitized this material with
the help of John Webb. The people who saved this film and got it to Dr. Hecla
are Lee Hite and David Carpenter. The late John Webb (W7NWH), Otto Woike, George
Pomeroy, and Gunnar Thornton contributed to the development and preservation of
this film.
This page contains a full transcript of the recordings with links to the specific
timestamps in the films.
Parts 1-4
Parts 5-7
For a more âvividâ view of the project, make sure to check out
this 1960 film
we got digitized showing the actual hardware these guys are talking about:
1 Intro
01:40
From 1946 through 51, the Fairchild Airplane Company conducted feasibility studies for nuclear propulsion for aircraft, or NEPA. Various cycles, power plants, and nuclear reactors were explored. Among the decisions was that the jet engine, still in its infancy, was to be used. In 1951, a decision was made that GEANP was to develop the direct cycle concept where the air from the compressor
02:09
was heated directly by the reactor fuel elements. Major elements of the ANP program are shown on the chart. During the 1951-53 early nuclear flight was an objective to determine operational feasibility of a nuclear-powered aircraft. The test aircraft was to be a B-36.
02:33
The power plant consisted of four modified J-47s designated the X-39. The energy was supplied by one R-1 reactor. The R-1 was water-moderated and had an aluminum structure. The fuel element consisted of a 310 stainless steel plus UO2 matrix, which was clad with stainless steel. The program was redirected in early 1953. Three heat transfer reactor experiments, HTREs, followed.
03:04
From 1952 through 61, the divided shield design was validated and various shield materials were tested in the tower shield facility at Oak Ridge. Also, 40 test flights of a B-36 with a small 2-megawatt thermal reactor aboard were conducted by Convair at Fort Worth. On January 31st of 1956, in the HTRE 1,
03:31
The first jet engine operated on nuclear power at the National Reactor Test Station in Idaho. The fuel material was nichrome plus UO2. Tests began in 1957 of the HTRE 2. It was similar in design to the HTRE 1, but with an 11-inch hole in the center of the core, where advanced fuel element and moderator designs were tested until 1961.
03:58
The HTRE 3 was built in a full-scale aircraft reactor configuration. It was tested using an air-cooled solid moderator, zirconium hydride, and nichrome with a few elements. Two X-39 engines were operated at full power. Nuclear starts were demonstrated. From 1956 through 59, the XMA-1A development program was to meet the Air Force Camel mission.
04:27
including supersonic sprint. New twin X-211 engines shared a reactor between them. A new solid moderator of yttrium hydride with capability of 2,300 degrees Fahrenheit was developed. However, the advanced fuel element, though structurally improved, did not yet have the capability of 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit turbine inlet temperature.
04:55
By 1959, development tests demonstrated that a BEO ceramic reactor would meet the 1,800 degree Fahrenheit turbine inlet temperature. The XNJ-140 power plant had one X-211 engine with a ceramic reactor. It provided 100 megawatts at cruise conditions. By March 1961, other competitive weapons systems such as missiles and nuclear submarines
05:24
had obviated the need for a nuclear-powered aircraft. Therefore, the A&P program was canceled. This is a model of a nuclear-powered jet engine, the XNJ-140. It is one-tenth scale. The actual engine was 37 feet in length. This is the compressor, the reactor with the shield assembly, the combustor,
05:53
the turbine, and the nozzle. By the end of 1960, 11 builds of the turbine machinery did operate in Cincinnati on chemical fuel. The XNJ-140 was scheduled to operate on nuclear power in 1962 at the National Reactor Test Station in Idaho.
06:33
This is a model of the Convair NX-2 aircraft. It was to fly in 1965. The canard configuration is well suited for a nuclear-powered aircraft. There are three XNJ-140 engines at the rear of the fuselage where they're accessible for remote handling and maintenance. 100 feet forward is the crew compartment, which is shielded.
07:03
Air inlets to the engines are located at the base of the wings. J-75s are mounted in pods and are used for takeoff only in the event of a loss of an engine. The hangar to house this aircraft and provide the remote maintenance was constructed in Idaho by April of 1961 when the Aircraft Nuclear Propulsion Program
07:33
was cancelled.
2.1 Back

data.title: After 25 Years, Linux Format Magazine Is No More
data.author: AdmiralAsshat
data.article_summary: 《Linux Format》杂志于2000年5月创刊，提供Linux及开源软件的新闻、评测、教程等内容，并附带光盘。25年后，该杂志宣布停刊，出版商Future未说明具体原因，但印刷媒体在数字内容时代的经济困境是主因。尽管一些杂志成功转型为数字版，其他则合并或减少发行，而《Linux Format》未能继续。其2014年的发行量为19,000份，之后数据未公开。停刊也反映了纸媒在当前环境下的生存挑战。对Linux爱好者而言，仍有《Linux Magazine》和《Raspberry Pi Magazine》等可供选择。文章作者通过该杂志首次接触Ubuntu，并因此创立了专注Ubuntu的博客。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：杂志行业的衰落及其原因，以及对印刷杂志的情感与记忆

不同观点：
• dcminter认为，尽管人们可能对某些杂志感兴趣，但由于杂志订阅和取消机制的问题，导致订阅体验不佳，进而影响订阅意愿。他指出，一些杂志存在不明确的取消机制或配送问题，可能自设障碍。
• weinzierl表达了对过去杂志的怀旧情感，提到杂志曾是他获取信息和逃避现实的唯一途径。然而，他也承认，某些杂志能存活至今让他感到意外，自己已经很久没有购买杂志。
• ChocolateGod和vmilner强调了特定杂志（如Linux Format）在技术领域的影响力，并对其停刊表示遗憾。ChocolateGod提到Linux Format引导他进入Linux世界，而vmilner则表示自己订阅该杂志长达20年。
• davidwritesbugs和leephillips作为曾为这些杂志撰稿的作者，表达了对杂志停刊的惋惜，特别是对高报酬和尊重作者版权的编辑团队的怀念。

补充讨论：
• treve询问是否有推荐的（小众）印刷杂志，显示出对定期收到实体邮件的兴趣。
• pjmlp提到报摊上的技术杂志今不如昔，反映了整个行业的变化。
• GuinansEyebrows深情回忆了各种曾喜爱的杂志，强调杂志不仅提供内容，还通过多样化的主题和精美的排版带来独特的阅读体验。他特别提到2600杂志的独立性和社区参与价值。
• unethical_ban以幽默方式指出，尽管从杂志中学到很多，但有些技术问题仍无法通过杂志解决。

44158658.article_content:
In May 2000, the first issue of a brand new Linux magazine hit British newsstands, delivering a monthly mix of news, reviews, interviews, tutorials and learned insight on all things free and open-source — plus that all-important cover-mounted CD/DVD!
Now, 25 years later, the final ever issue has gone on sale.
Future
, the UK-based publisher of Linux Format, hasn’t said why the magazine is closing, but one needn’t consult an
Oracular Oriole
to divine the reason: the economics of making print publishing work in an age of digital-first content is hard.
So, in a way, the writing is less on the pages and more on the wall for dead-tree media in general. It’s a topic I could talk about—’old man shouts at clouds’ style—at length.
Fact is: if people wanted magazines on topics they care about (along with the wider industries, jobs, skills, opportunities and public service those magazines support) to survive, they’d buy ’em.
But with no algorithms to surface dopamine-inducing stories; no verifiable engagement rates to game for investor approval; and no ability to provide on-demand AI summaries to free up time so readers can do more doom-scrolling on social media
1
, it’s unlikely.
FYIDYK!
It was a double-sided live DVD included in
Linux Format
issue 103 (March 2008) that introduced me to Ubuntu. The disc had bootable live sessions of
OpenSUSE
,
PCLinux OS
, and
Ubuntu
. I tried
OpenSUSE
first but it didn’t run properly. I booted the next OS, Ubuntu 7.10
‘Gutsy Gibbon’
— the rest is history!
Ubuntu 8.04 LTS arrived about 3 weeks later and, after upgrading, my enthusiasm for the distro deepened. I started to share Ubuntu tips and tricks on my personal blog, as well as news on changes that were being planned for the then-upcoming Ubuntu 8.10 release. That stuff resonated to the point that, a month later, I decided to split my Ubuntu coverage out into a separate Ubuntu-focused blog.
That blog? The one you’re reading right now!
As said, there is—as of writing—no formal reason why Linux Format is ceasing publication after 25 years in print, nor much word I could find from the current folks who edit and produce the magazine.
It’s not a given that proper editorial publications are doomed to die, either.
In fact, recent years have seen a number of once leading niche magazines pivot from print to digital editions, many to great success. Other magazines merged with rivals, reduced page (and head) count, or shifted to a slower schedule to keep their dream alive.
The last reported circulation figures for
Linux Format
from ABC (the ‘Audited Bureau of Circulation’ in the UK) are from 2014. Back then, Linux Format was was shifting around 19,000 physical copies a month.
Naturally, the figure will have dropped, but as none of Future’s print or digital titles appear to be audited by ABC, we’ve no figures
2
to say how much — though clearly
too much
for Linux Format’s publisher to feel it worth continuing the title — not even digital-only.
For media companies with broad portfolios and demands to increase revenue, sentiment and ideals don’t factor too much.
When I was doing
OMG! Linux
, I
ran a couple of posts to spotlight
new issues of Linux Format. A few readers thought they were paid ads (they weren’t) so I stopped. And
Future
weren’t interested
3
in making it easier for me to promote their title, either.
Linux Format’s first issue
Linux Format’s First Issue
Linux Format’s first issue went on sale in May 2000 priced at £4.99. It came with cover-mount CD of
Definite Linux 7.0
, backed by a 10 page guide to using the distro within the magazine itself.
There were also 25 pages of tutorials and tips, features on networking with Macs, open-source licensing, and a distro rating guide. Rather cute: a mail-away promotion from SuSE offered readers of the first issue a free CD of SuSE Linux 1!
If you’re interested in reading the first issue of Linux Format, you can
download a PDF of it here
.
As someone who didn’t start using any flavour of Linux until 2008, that first issue is a real time capsule of how the more things change, the more they stay the same.
Any Linux magazines still going?
Linux enthusiasts who enjoy the mindful, intentional experience of sitting down to read a magazine dedicated to Linux, free of the hysteria, algorithmic manipulation or gamified engagement tactics found online, have choices.
Linux Magazine
is still in print, and though it’s not a magazine I’ve bought before, I will make an effort to grab a copy. The official
Raspberry Pi Magazine
is also still in print for those seeking a more focused Linux-related read.
The final issue of
Linux Format
is on sale now if you fancy picking up a copy
— assuming there’s somewhere near you that still stocks magazines…
Aka being “more productive”.
↩︎
In 2024, the combined average monthly circulation of magazines audited by ABC (which does NOT include many of the best selling magazines, since their publishers won’t want the figures public) stood at 18.7 million,
per Press Gazette
. In

data.title: Workers Want a Four-Day Week. Companies Should Too
data.author: lxm
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：四天工作制的可行性及其在不同行业和岗位上的适用性

不同观点：
• windows2020：认为四天工作制可能通过减缓工作节奏或增加人手来实现，并提到这可能会促进招聘，给员工更多谈判筹码。该观点偏向支持四天工作制，认为它可以带来积极的改变。

• philipallstar：对四天工作制的普遍适用性提出质疑，指出该制度可能仅适用于任务导向型工作，而服务业等需要员工在顾客可能出现的每一天都工作。此外，提到如果人们能在四天内完成五天的工作，是否也能在三天内完成四天的工作，从而对四天工作制的长期有效性提出疑问。该观点较为中立，关注实际操作中的困难和长期影响。

• NotAnOtter：认为讨论四天工作制在英语论坛中过于热门，并指出许多独立贡献者（IC's）的工作本质上是异步的，甚至可以压缩到一天内完成。提到其公司实行无会议周五，并且远程工作让他可以灵活安排时间。质疑企业为何要激励员工少工作或强制他们进入已经可选的日程安排。该观点偏向怀疑四天工作制对企业的实际意义。

• doesnotexist：提到冰岛已经成功实施了四天工作制，暗示该制度在实际中是可行的，并提供了一个参考链接。该观点支持四天工作制的可行性。

• mitchbob：提供了一个华尔街日报文章的存档链接，可能用于支持其观点，但未明确陈述其立场。

• oldpersonintx2：以讽刺的语气指出，如果工人有了新获得的周五休息日，他们可能会出去消费，而这些消费场所仍需要员工来服务。该观点反对四天工作制，认为会带来服务行业的员工短缺问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是四天工作制在不同行业和岗位上的适用性，特别是服务行业和客户 facing 角色的覆盖问题。
• 另一个争议点是四天工作制的长期有效性，以及是否会导致工作范围缩小至三天甚至更少。
• 讨论中还涉及企业是否有动力去减少员工工作时间，以及如何平衡员工的个人生活和工作需求。

data.title: Tabletop particle blaster: Tiny nozzles, lasers could replace giant accelerators
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 研究人员在大阪大学的领导下，开发出一种名为微喷嘴加速（MNA）的新技术，通过使用微小喷嘴结构和超强超短激光脉冲，成功生成高质量的吉电子伏特（GeV）级质子束。与传统方法只能达到100兆电子伏特（MeV）以下的能量限制不同，MNA方法利用准静电场，使质子能量突破1 GeV，且具有出色的束流质量和稳定性。这一突破有望应用于紧凑型激光核聚变、精准质子癌症治疗以及模拟极端天体物理环境，标志着粒子加速器技术向小型化和高效率迈出了重要一步。研究成果已发表在《Scientific Reports》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高能武器的技术与潜力，特别是质子步枪与激光武器的比较。

不同观点：
• 观点一：[mpoteat] 认为高能质子步枪可能比现有的高能激光武器更强大。他通过类比高能激光器已经能够做到的高度集中能量输出，推测如果玻色子流（如激光）能造成如此大的伤害，那么强子流（如质子）可能会有更大的破坏力。这个观点强调了质子武器的潜在威力。

• 观点二：隐含的反对方观点可能认为现有的高能激光武器已经是非常先进的技术，可能对质子步枪的实际效用和可行性持怀疑态度。虽然没有直接的反对言论，但通过强调激光武器的成熟度，可以推测出对新概念武器（如质子步枪）的实际优势持保留态度。

补充讨论：
• 类比论据：[mpoteat] 使用了高能激光武器作为对比，提出了对质子步枪威力的假设。这种类比有助于理解质子步枪的潜在能力，但也可能存在不准确的地方，因为激光和质子在物理性质和工作原理上有显著差异。

• 争议焦点：争议的焦点可能在于质子步枪的实际可行性和相对于现有技术（如激光武器）的优势。虽然质子武器在理论上可能有优势，但其技术实现、实用性和性价比等方面可能存在质疑。

• 物理原理：讨论涉及到基本的物理概念，如玻色子（如光子）和强子（如质子）的区别。理解这两类粒子的不同特性对于评估两类武器的潜力非常重要。

June 2, 2025
The GIST
Tabletop particle blaster: How tiny nozzles and lasers could replace giant accelerators
by University of Osaka
edited by
Lisa Lock
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
peer-reviewed publication
proofread
Conceptual illustration of micronozzle acceleration (MNA). A solid hydrogen rod is embedded in an aluminum micronozzle, which channels and focuses plasma flow to optimize proton acceleration. Credit: Masakatsu Murakami
Proton beams with giga-electron-volt (GeV) energies—once thought to be achievable only with massive particle accelerators—may soon be generated in compact setups thanks to a breakthrough by researchers at The University of Osaka.
A team led by Professor Masakatsu Murakami has developed a novel concept called micronozzle acceleration (MNA). By designing a microtarget with tiny nozzle-like features and irradiating it with ultraintense, ultrashort laser pulses, the team successfully demonstrated—through advanced numerical simulations—the generation of high-quality, GeV-class proton beams: a world-first achievement.
The article, "Generation of giga-electron-volt proton beams by micronozzle acceleration," was
published
in
Scientific Reports
.
Unlike traditional laser-based acceleration methods that use flat targets and reach energy limits below 100 mega-electron-volt (MeV), the micronozzle structure enables sustained, stepwise acceleration of protons within a powerful quasi-static electric field created inside the target. This new mechanism allows proton energies to exceed 1 GeV, with excellent
beam
quality and stability.
"This discovery opens a new door for compact, high-efficiency particle acceleration," says Prof. Murakami. "We believe this method has the potential to revolutionize fields such as laser fusion
energy
, advanced radiotherapy, and even laboratory-scale astrophysics."
Concept of micronozzle acceleration (MNA). The MNA target employs a micronozzle housing a solid hydrogen rod (H-rod), precisely placed near the nozzle neck to maximize proton yield. Acting as a "power lens," the micronozzle focuses the incident laser energy onto the H-rod, enabling efficient and localized energy deposition. This configuration significantly boosts proton acceleration near the nozzle exit, outperforming setups lacking the nozzle structure. Credit:
Scientific Reports
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41598-025-03385-x
The implications are wide-reaching:
Energy: Supports fast ignition schemes in laser-driven nuclear fusion.
Medicine: Enables more compact and precise systems for proton cancer therapy.
Fundamental science: Creates conditions to simulate extreme astrophysical environments and probe matter under ultra-strong magnetic fields.
The study, based on simulations performed on the SQUID supercomputer at The University of Osaka, marks the first-ever theoretical demonstration of compact GeV
proton
acceleration using microstructured targets.
More information:
M. Murakami et al, Generation of giga-electron-volt proton beams by micronozzle acceleration,
Scientific Reports
(2025).
DOI: 10.1038/s41598-025-03385-x

data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在设计Rust库的错误类型时需要考虑的重要因素和常见误区，特别关注公共API的设计。对于二进制 crate，通常使用 `anyhow` 或 `eyre` 处理错误即可，因为不需要对外暴露错误类型。而对于库 crate，则需要仔细设计错误类型，确保其可被其他 crate 使用且不引入不必要的依赖。

常见设计方式有两种：
1. 使用 `thiserror` crate，通过 `#[from]` 转换其他错误类型，减少样板代码。
2. 像 `std::io::Error` 那样定义包含 `ErrorKind` 的自定义错误类型。

文中还提到一个常见错误是“内部错误类型泄露”，即直接暴露第三方库的错误类型（如 `sqlx::Error`），导致库的使用者需额外依赖这些第三方库。为解决此问题，建议使用 trait 对象（如 `Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>`）封装内部错误，从而避免不必要的依赖和版本冲突，同时保持API的灵活性。

不同观点：
• [saghm 的观点] 认为使用 trait 对象（如 `dyn Error`）而不是具体错误类型，可以提供更大的灵活性。例如，可以选择不同的容器（如 `Arc`）来满足多线程环境下的需求。他举例说明在处理后台线程错误时，使用 `Arc` 包裹 `dyn Error` 简化了并发场景下的错误处理逻辑。虽然这种情况不常见，但展示了 Rust API 设计的可组合性优势。

• [vlovich123 的观点] 提出了一种避免使用 `Box` 进行类型隐藏的技巧，即使用不透明公共类型来包裹私有类型。通过具体例子展示了如何使用 `struct` 和 `enum` 来实现这一点，并指出虽然需要在结果处理时使用 `.map_error`，但总体上并不麻烦。这表明具体错误类型在某些情况下可以提供更好的性能和可控性。

• [saghm 的观点] 强调了在特定场景下（如多线程错误追踪），`dyn Error` 的灵活性和可组合性带来的实际好处。虽然这种情况不普遍，但对某些复杂需求提供了有效解决方案。

• [vlovich123 的观点] 则更关注于在不牺牲性能的情况下实现类型隐藏，提出了一个更为常见的解决方案，并指出了实现上的一些小麻烦，但认为这是可接受的。

44156843.article_content:
When designing error types in Rust, especially for libraries with a public API, there are several important considerations to keep in mind. This post will explore some of the important implications and common pitfalls when designing error types in Rust libraries. Further, we will look at
thiserror
and how the Rust standard library's
std::io::Error
can serve as a reference for designing your own error types.
Library vs. Binary crate
When designing error types in Rust, it's important to consider whether your code is part of a library or a binary. The design principles can differ significantly between the two.
Usually for a binary crate, you simply use crates like
anyhow
or
eyre
to handle errors, because your main goal is often to provide a good user error message and you don't need to expose your error types to other crates. So there is no need to design a custom error type unless you want to
match
on it in your code or log it differently than you would present it to the user.
For a library crate, however, you want to design your error types carefully, as they will be part of the public API and will be used by other crates. This means you should consider how your error types will be used, what information they will provide, and how they will interact with other error types in the ecosystem.
Usually there are two main approaches to designing error types in Rust libraries:
Using
thiserror
crate
: This is a popular choice for library crates, as it provides a convenient way to define error types with minimal boilerplate. It allows you to derive the
std::error::Error
trait and provides a way to convert other error types into your custom error type using the
#[from]
attribute.
Using a self-defined error type
similar to
std::io::Error
and
ErrorKind
: This approach involves defining a custom error type with an enum that represents different error variants.
Each variant would be very plain and only used on one very specific occasion and not carry any additional information. The error struct would then implement the
std::error::Error
trait and associate the
ErrorKind
variant with the source error (
see the std lib
).
Using
thiserror
with
#[from]
The
thiserror
crate is a popular choice for defining error types in Rust libraries. It allows you to derive the
std::error::Error
trait and provides a convenient way to convert other error types into your custom error type using the
#[from]
attribute. This can significantly reduce boilerplate code and make error handling more ergonomic and implementation time efficient.
Common mistake: inner error type leakage
Imagine you write a library that uses a crate like
sqlx
or
reqwest
and you have an error variant that looks like this:
#[
derive
(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum
MyError {
#[
error
("
Database error: {0}
")]
DatabaseError(#[
from
] sqlx::Error),
#[
error
("
Network error: {0}
")]
NetworkError(#[
from
] reqwest::Error),
}
This might seem like a reasonable approach at first glance, as it allows you to convert the inner error types into your custom error type using the
#[from]
attribute.
However, this design has a significant drawback: it leaks the inner error types (
sqlx::Error
and
reqwest::Error
) to your library consumers.
So unless you are re-exporting these error types (and the types they use and expose), a library consumer will have to depend on
sqlx
and
reqwest
crates to use these error variants, even if they never use the database or network functionality directly.
This is bad design because it imposes unnecessary dependencies on your library users and increases the complexity.
Furthermore, this can lead to version mismatch issues. For example, if you depend on
sqlx
version 0.5.0, but your library user depends on
sqlx
version 0.6.0, then they will run into compilation errors and they're forced to downgrade their
sqlx
version to match your used version, which is really problematic.
Solution: Boxing the inner error type as a trait object
A better approach is to avoid exposing the inner error types directly in your library's error type. Instead, you can use a boxed trait object to encapsulate the inner error types. This way, your library users won't have to depend on
sqlx
or
reqwest
, and you can still provide meaningful error messages.
#[
derive
(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum
MyError {
#[
error
("
Database error: {0}
")]
DatabaseError(#[
from
] Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>),
#[
error
("
Network error: {0}
")]
NetworkError(#[
from
] Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>),
}
This creates an opaque error type that can hold any error that implements the
std::error::Error
trait, while still allowing you to provide a meaningful error message and providing access to the inner error message via the
Display
implementation and even the underlying error type through dynamic downcasting if needed.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：0.999... 是否等于 1，以及如何用不同数学框架解释该问题。

不同观点：
• [tsimionescu] 认为0.999... 只是分数的记号表示，并不是真正的数。在学校教授的分数为主的数学体系中，0.999... 被视为不合理的表示法，且无限小数运算被认为是不严谨的。该观点强调分数是“真实”的有理数表示，而小数只是简写。

• [bubblyworld] 引入了超实数的概念，指出在超实数体系中，0.999... 可以等于 1 减去一个无穷小量 (1 - eps)。然而，当考虑所有自然数（包括非标准自然数）时，0.999... 仍然等于 1。该观点认为原作者在数学理解上存在混淆，尤其是在非标准分析和转移原理的应用上。

• [quitit] 指出学生常陷入自相矛盾的理解，即接受 0.333... 等于 1/3，但不接受 0.999... 等于 1。该观点强调需要一致地应用分数和小数之间的转换规则，以消除困惑。

• [lcrz] 批评原作者试图通过超实数来解释 0.999... 与 1 的不等式，认为这是误导。实际上，在实数体系中，0.999... 严格等于 1，并不存在无穷小差异。

• [cbolton] 强调应正确理解 0.999... 的定义，即通过极限的概念来解释。该观点认为一旦理解了小数表示的极限含义，就不会再有是否等于 1 的疑问。

• [mr_mitm] 指出，在构造实数时，可以通过Cauchy序列或Maclaurin级数来明确0.999... 和 1 是同一数的不同表示形式。在抽象意义上，它们属于同一等价类，但表示方式不同。

• [fouronnes3] 提供了一个简单的证明思路，即在 0.999... 和 1 之间不存在其他数，因此它们必须是同一个数。

• [beyondCritics] 解释0.999... 是数字字符串的加权和，其定义为部分和的极限。该观点强调了德国高中数学教育中对极限概念的普及。

补充讨论：
• [neeeeeeal] 表达了对HN社区多样化讨论的赞赏，但未直接讨论数学问题。
• [HourglassFR] 认为原作者试图通过非直观的方式解释问题，但引入了更复杂的概念（如超实数），反而使问题更混乱。
• [A_D_E_P_T] 提到了一篇旧的Arxiv论文，认为其直觉上是正确的。
• [quchen] 批评了在基本数学问题中引入超实数的做法，认为这是不必要的混淆。
• [dominicrose] 认为无穷数学和概率论中的一些概念难以通过理性思维理解。
• [constantcrying] 强调了实数相等的定义，指出0.999... 和 1 相等的根本原因在于它们在实数体系中的等价类相同。
• [yodsanklai] 指出理解数与数表示之间的区别是关键，0.999... 和 1 是同一数的两不同表示。

争议焦点：主要集中在是否可以通过超实数体系解释0.999... 与1的不等式，以及如何在实数体系中严格定义和理解这一等式。不同观点之间的核心分歧在于是否接受小数表示的无穷序列作为合理的数学对象。

主要讨论点：评论围绕一组乐器内部照片的互动游戏、摄影技术、视觉效果及艺术感受展开讨论。

不同观点：
• [susam] 提出一个互动游戏：通过开发者工具使文本透明，然后猜测图片代表的乐器，并分享了自己的得分。这表明评论者关注的是与内容的互动体验以及猜测的乐趣。
• [pimlottc] 分享了更多照片的链接，引导其他用户查看，侧重于提供更多视觉资源。
• [rwmj] 将小提琴的内部结构与历史上著名船只的甲板进行比较，提供了一个外部链接以作参考，强调了视觉上的相似性。
• [account42] 质疑为何不使用针孔相机来拍摄这些静态物体，并建议通过长时间曝光和多重曝光来减少噪点，关注的是摄影技术的选择。
• [HarHarVeryFunny] 对小提琴内部的不规则性表示兴趣，并提出是否对称的内部结构会产生更好的音效，涉及到乐器设计与音质的关联。
• [ubj] 表达了对照片的喜爱，并幻想建造一个类似照片风格的音乐厅，侧重于艺术感受和设计灵感。
• [hinkley] 提出了一种使用镜子和小孔进行拍摄的替代方法，详细描述了具体操作步骤，关注的是摄影技术的改进。
• [izzydata] 对照片的尺度感提出疑问，并将其与自己可能的拍摄结果进行对比，关注的是视觉效果的尺度感知。
• [e40] 对dpreview网站的重启表示高兴，并询问谁拯救了该网站，讨论点偏离了主要内容，转向网站历史。
• [yard2010] 赞美照片的美学，同时批评页面上的广告，形成了对比，强调了视觉体验的对比感受。
• [gnabgib] 提供了之前相关讨论的链接，引导读者查看历史讨论，侧重于提供背景信息。
• [sandspar] 以一种轻松的语气表达了对昆虫世界的羡慕，属于个人情感的表达，与主要讨论点关系不大。
• [coreyp_1] 分享了自己购买照片的经历，并表示有意再次购买，涉及到个人体验和对摄影作品的欣赏。
• [ErigmolCt] 将照片效果比作外星建筑或反乌托邦城市，强调了照片的超现实和艺术性。
• [colordrops] 将照片与游戏《The Room》中的场景联系起来，强调了视觉上的联想和游戏体验。

- 其他值得注意的讨论点：一些评论如[e40] 和 [sandspar] 偏离了主要讨论点，但增添了对话的趣味性和广度。

44157568.article_content:
AttendList
Chrome Extension
Login
Start tracking →
←
Home
//
Published 2nd June, 2025
Our Production Ruby on Rails Stack
AttendList is an
attendance tracker for Google Meet
. It's built on a
Ruby on Rails
backend that talks to a
Chrome Extension
.
This article explores the infrastructure and gem choices I've made while building AttendList, from the basics like
background jobs
,
auth
and
blogging
, to
deployment
and some
fun extras
.
Table of contents:
The basics (PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, RSpec)
Authentication (Devise, OAuth)
View layer (Tailwind CSS and ViewComponents)
Performance and Profiling (Bullet, Rack Mini Profiler)
Google APIs
Blogging (Custom)
Hosting and deployment (Hatchbox)
Extras (Dashboard, Charts, DevX etc)
Conclusion
The basics (PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, RSpec)
gem
"pg"
# database
gem
"redis"
# cache
gem
"sidekiq"
# background jobs
gem
"rspec-rails"
# testing
gem
"factory_bot_rails"
# test data
AttendList's core stack is
pretty vanilla
— it uses
PostgreSQL
for the database,
Redis
for caching and job queues, and
Sidekiq
for background jobs.
This is the stack I use for all my side-projects. It's rock-solid, reliable and
cheap to host
.
I veer slightly off the "Rails way" with
RSpec
&
factories
for tests, but that's just a preference thing.
Authentication (Devise, OAuth)
gem
"devise"
# Auth
gem
"activerecord-session_store"
# Session storage
gem
"omniauth-rails_csrf_protection"
# Make Oauth and Devise play together nicely
gem
"omniauth-google-oauth2"
# Support "login with Google"
gem
"pretender"
# Devise impersonation
An AttendList user logs in through a
Devise
login flow via
Google OAuth
.
AttendList then asks users to re-auth with Google to connect Google Meet (ie: grant necessary scopes), via an
incremental authorization flow
. It's an auth style that
Google encourages
where you initially
only
request the minimal scopes from a user (ie: name & email), then
re-request more scopes
as needed.
An incremental auth flow with Devise looks a bit like this:
button_to
(
user_google_oauth2_omniauth_authorize_path
(
scope:
"..."
,
prompt:
"consent"
,
include_granted_scopes:
"true"
,
login_hint:
current_user
.
email
,
),
data:
{
turbo:
false
})
do
>>>
Connect
Google
Meet
<<<
end
This prompts a user to OAuth again via Google — thereby granting additional scopes — after they've initially logged in.
Finally, I use the
Pretender gem
to login as different users within AttendList, for support & debugging.
View layer (Tailwind CSS and ViewComponents)
gem
"tailwindcss-rails"
# use TailwindCSS
gem
"view_component"
# better version of partials
gem
"rails_icons"
# easily use various icon libraries
I've been a big fan of
ViewComponent
for years now, and I use them heavily in all my apps. I've
written about ViewComponents before
; they plug in very neatly to the standard Rails stack, feel excellent to work with and are a huge step up from regular partials.
For styling, I use
Tailwind CSS
. It helps me style UIs extremely quickly, and it plays nicely with Rails and ViewComponent.
I lean heavily on
TailwindUI
for UI components, and pair it with the
Phosphor icon library
(via the
rails_icons gem
gem). I previously defaulted to
Heroicons
for icons, but Phosphor has vastly more icons available.
Performance and Profiling (Bullet, Rack Mini Profiler)
gem
"rack-mini-profiler"
# Page rendering insights, SQL counts etc
gem
"bullet"
# Automatically alerts for N+1 queries
I use the
Bullet
gem to catch N+1 queries, and combine it with
rack-mini-profiler
to keep an eye on performance. Both are handy and painless to setup.
I only run these gems in the
development
environment, but I saw recently that
Campsite used to run rack-mini-profiler in production
, which I might look into.
Google APIs
gem
"googleauth"
gem
"google-apps-meet-v2"
gem
"google-apis-people_v1"
Google has a
bunch of Ruby client libraries
, and I use these three for AttendList.
There's not much to say here — they work fine; they're auto-generated, so they can feel a bit clunky to use, but it's not too bad.
Blogging (Custom)
gem
"redcarpet"
# markdown parsing
gem
"rouge"
# code highlighting
gem
"sitemap_generator"
# sitemap builder
gem
"front_matter_parser"
# parse frontmatter from .md files
I've rolled my own blogging system for AttendList.
Its cornerstone is the
Redcarpet
gem. Redcarpet powers all the markdown rendering, which I pipe through a Tailwind CSS
prose
class
to neatly format each blog post.
I pair Redcarpet with
Rouge
for code highlighting (like above), using the included plugin for Redcarpet and the
base16.solarized.light
theme (
preview other themes
).
I also use the
Sitemap Generator
gem to create an XML sitemap, and
front-matter-parser
to extract data from each post, like the title & published_at date.
Hosting and deployment (Hatchbox)
I use
Hatchbox
to deploy AttendList and host on servers from
Hetzner
.
Hetzner is absurdly good value — I'm using a single
CAX31
instance, with
8 vCPU
cores,
16 GB
of RAM,
160 GB
of storage and
20 TB
of bandwidth...
